articles.title: Who is Sara Smith? Mystery Ole Miss fan goes viral after ESPN captures her reaction during Louisville game
articles.summary: International Sports News: One ESPN camera cut was all it took to turn an unidentified Ole Miss fan into the newest viral sensation in college football. During Ole Miss’ dramati.
articles.body: One ESPN camera cut was all it took to turn an unidentified Ole Miss fan into the newest viral sensation in college football. During Ole Miss’ dramatic 41–38 victory over Louisville on Sept. 6, cameras caught a blonde fan in the stands reacting to the action, and within hours, social media was flooded with questions about who she was.Mystery blonde Ole Miss fan goes viral on ESPN, internet thinks it knows who she isThe moment came during the third quarter as Louisville mounted pressure on the Rebels. The fan was seen holding her phone above her head before suddenly putting her hands on her head as the tension inside the stadium intensified.That brief reaction quickly escaped the broadcast, with fans asking the same question: Who is the mystery Ole Miss girl?As the clip spread, internet sleuths began attempting to identify the woman.Several social-media accounts circulated the name Sara Smith, with some claiming that a private Instagram account belonging to a Sara M. Smith was the viral fan.Reports have also linked the account to an Ole Miss alum from Knoxville.However, there is an important caveat: Smith herself has not publicly confirmed that she is the woman seen in the ESPN footage. The Instagram account believed by social-media users to belong to her is private, meaning many of the claims circulating online cannot independently be verified.For now, the identification should therefore be treated as unconfirmed, rather than fact. Regardless of her identity, the reaction became one of the most talked-about fan moments of the weekend.The fascination is familiar in the social-media era. A fan can appear on television for only a few seconds before thousands of viewers begin searching for their name, Instagram, and background.That is exactly what happened here.The mystery surrounding the woman has arguably become almost as interesting as the original clip, with fans trying to piece together her identity while the woman at the center of the attention has not publicly addressed the sudden spotlight.And the timing made the moment even better.Ole Miss eventually escaped with a 41–38 win, with Lucas Carneiro drilling a 48-yard field goal as time expired.So what initially looked like a devastating moment for the Rebels fan ultimately ended with a victory.For now, the internet may have a name, but that does not necessarily mean the mystery is officially solved. Until the woman herself confirms her identity or a reliable source independently verifies it, claims that the viral fan is Sara Smith should remain attributed and qualified.What is certain is that an ordinary night in the Ole Miss stands turned into an unexpected moment of internet fame.And with college football season only getting started, the mystery blonde fan may have already become one of the sport's first viral stars of 2026.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jordan Ayew: Sheffield United sign veteran forward on deal to end of season
articles.summary: Sheffield United sign former Crystal Palace and Leicester City forward Jordan Ayew on a deal until the end of the season.
articles.body:
Sheffield United have signed former Crystal Palace and Leicester City forward Jordan Ayew on a deal until the end of the season.

The 34-year-old, who has won 124 caps for Ghana, was a free agent after leaving the Foxes at the end of last season following their relegation to League One.

Ayew joined Aston Villa from Lorient in 2015 and has spent the past 11 years in the Premier League and Championship.

"We're talking about someone here with bags of experience from right at the top level of the game," boss Chris Wilder told the club website. , external

"Only a few months ago he was captaining Ghana in the World Cup, so he's someone with real pedigree.

"He did well at this level last season in difficult circumstances and has played all across the front positions during his career which gives us plenty of options."

Meanwhile, Blades defender Nils Zatterstrom and midfielder Ehije Ukaki, both 21, have gone on season-long loans to Polish side Rakow Czestochowa and Bulgarian club Botev Plovdiv respectively.

Swede Zatterstrom has not featured for United since joining last August, while Nigerian Ukaki, who joined from Plovdiv in June last year, made his sole appearance in a Carabao Cup defeat by Birmingham City in August 2025.

articles.title: Piqué blinda al juvenil Tiago Olmedo hasta junio de 2030
articles.standfirst: El lateral de 18 años fue convocado en los tres primeros partidos de Segunda contra Ceuta, Celta y Eibar
articles.summary: El lateral de 18 años fue convocado en los tres primeros partidos de Segunda contra Ceuta, Celta y Eibar
articles.body: El Andorra ha blindado a Tiago Olmedo hasta junio de 2030. El joven lateral de Manresa, todavía en edad juvenil, se encuentra, desde este verano, en dinámica del primer equipo, "una muestra de la confianza que el club deposita en su progresión", han citado desde la entidad tricolor. De hecho, aunque todavía no ha debutado oficialmente con el primer equipo, Olmedo seguirá compaginando los entrenamientos con la primera plantilla pirenaica y el conjunto juvenil del Nàstic de Manresa en División de Honor, manteniendo así su proceso de crecimiento. “Ha sido un cambio radical tanto en mi vida como futbolísticamente. Es una experiencia inolvidable que siento que tengo que aprovechar al máximo", ha dicho el futbolista justo después de renovar. "Individualmente quiero tomar todos los aprendizajes y conceptos que pueda, y espero aportar al máximo para que el grupo vaya lo mejor posible", ha añadido un Olmedo muy ilusionado con su presente y futuro como tricolor. Toda su corta trayectoria la ha hecho en su Manresa natal, empezando en el CE Manresa en categoría cadete para posteriormente dar el salto al Gimnàstic de Manresa hasta ahora. Este año, con el filial tricolor, el joven de 18 años ya ha disputado un duelo, el de la jornada inaugural de la División de Honor juvenil, en un triunfo por 0-1 ante el Racing Zaragoza. Esta temporada, además, ha sido convocado con el Andorra en los tres primeros partidos de Segunda División, contra Ceuta, Celta Fortuna y Eibar, sin llegar a disputar minutos en ninguno.

articles.title: SE Dons amateur goalkeeper could be next in line for Ugandan throne
articles.summary: A goalkeeper from an amateur team in South East London could become king of a Ugandan region after the death of his cousin.
articles.body:
An amateur goalkeeper, a vacant throne in a kingdom of Uganda and the search for a new king.

Is this likely to be the most remarkable story of the season?

South East Dons - founded in 2014 by British rapper Andrew 'Don Strapzy' McHugh - are arguably one of the most well-known amateur football clubs in the UK.

And given the situation surrounding their current captain and goalkeeper - George Desmond Kamurasi - that's unlikely to change anytime soon.

The BBC understands the SE Dons player is currently in Uganda to attend the funeral of King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV , which is expected to take place before the weekend.

As is tradition, his successor will be named before the burial - and it has been widely reported Kamurasi has been chosen as the region's new king.

Uganda is governed by an elected president and parliament, but it has several traditional kingdoms that continue to have significant cultural influence despite not having political power.

The Tooro Kingdom in western Uganda was ruled by King Oyo from 1995. He died in the United States last week, aged 34, after receiving treatment for an aggressive form of cancer.

Kamurasi, 36, is a direct descendant of the clan of 'Babiito' and cousin to the late King Oyo.

'I appeal to all Ugandans to remain patient'

It's a far cry from Bexleyheath in south east London, where Kamurasi has been a key member of the SE Dons team's quest to climb the footballing ladder.

The club recently garnered attention by reaching the second qualifying round of the FA Cup. They are due to play Chichester City on Saturday, 19 September.

Although Kamurasi is yet to comment on the reports, he took to social media to plead for patience and space in relation to the situation.

Writing on X , external he said: "I appeal to all Ugandans to remain patient and allow the Omusuuga and the committee to perform their duties in accordance with our cultural traditions for enthroning a new Omukama.

"Let us focus entirely on mourning my cousin, His Majesty King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV."

King Oyo was the world's youngest serving monarch, having ascended the throne at the age of three.

The vacant throne for the Tooro Kingdom of Uganda has courted much intrigue and speculation.

The Royal Select Committee, which is tasked with confirming a new king, must first create a shortlist that not only includes lineage through bloodlines but also relatives of the deceased monarch.

As is tradition, King Oyo's casket will be escorted to the royal burial grounds with his successor and a few close relatives.

The ceremony will also see the new king throw nine coffee beans into the ground where King Oyo is buried.

Before heading to the palace, where he will have a special meal cooked by someone selected specially to prepare it, he is also expected to 'battle' with someone for the throne.

In the past, all rulers of the region have lived in the area - and in the history of the Tooro Kingdom no-one has ever refused to take the throne.

Although, if that were to be the case, the Royal Select Committee would gather again to choose the next suitable candidate until a successor accepts.

Additional reporting by Bella Twine, from BBC World Service's Focus on Africa programme.

articles.title: Southeastern Conference Leaders to Discuss Kicking LSU Out of League over Player Eligibility Dispute
articles.summary: Leaders of the Southeastern Conference will meet Thursday to discuss whether to take the extraordinary step of kicking LSU out of the league in the wake of an ugly feud over whether players who spent time in the NFL should be allowed back on the team's roster this season.
articles.body:
Leaders of the Southeastern Conference will meet Thursday to discuss whether to take the extraordinary step of kicking LSU out of the league in the wake of an ugly feud over whether players who spent time in the NFL should be allowed back on the team's roster this season.

On Tuesday, the SEC amended the federal lawsuit it filed against LSU last week , asking the judge in the case to issue a temporary restraining order to prevent the school from taking action to block or interfere with the Thursday meeting of university presidents and chancellors.

A vote of at least two-thirds of the conference's CEOs would be needed to dump LSU, which is a founding member of the conference that was started in 1933. A declaration that Commissioner Greg Sankey included with the league's legal filing made the planned meeting sound like more than posturing. In it, Sankey said school presidents met to discuss the LSU situation last Friday.

"The consensus ... was and continues to be that LSU's continued membership in the conference would be inconsistent with the publicly stated values and principles of the conference and its remaining member institutions" even if LSU doesn't put the former NFL players on its roster, he said.

An LSU spokesman declined immediate comment.

The SEC established a rule forbidding teams to bring players with NFL experience back on their roster. But last Friday, a judge in Baton Rouge barred the league from enforcing it, a decision that was heartily celebrated by Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry and the state attorney general, Liz Murrill, who was added as a defendant. Murrill called the SEC's lawsuit "legal garbage" shortly after it was filed last week.

Two of the players, Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright, have been practicing with the team but were not placed on the roster in advance of last Saturday's 51-10 win over Clemson. They still could be added, and Sankey made note of two roster spots that have been left open for that possibility.

In a statement, the SEC said it has the right to establish rules and "a commitment to those rules and to the core principles of the Southeastern Conference is an essential element of SEC membership."

"Today's filing is necessary to defend that right and preserve the Conference's ability to govern competition among its members," the statement said.

Sankey took it a step further, saying in his declaration that SEC presidents were concerned LSU's president, Wade Rousse, and athletic director Verge Ausberry had no "meaningful control" over new coach Lane Kiffin or the football program.

"In light of the recalcitrance, lack of institutional control, and serious harm caused by the statements and conduct of LSU," the school presidents, other than Rousse, called for the meeting, Sankey said.

He said the meeting was to consider kicking out LSU "whether LSU renounces its intention to roster and play professional players on its football team, or not."

articles.title: Oporto - Manchester City en directo | Última hora de Champions League en vivo hoy
articles.summary: SE ACABÓ EL PARTIDO EN DO DRAGAO. GANÓ EL MANCHESTER CITY AL OPORTO POR 0-2. GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOL DE HAALAAAAAND. DOBLETEEEEEEEE. CINCO MINUTOS DE AÑAD
articles.body:
Última hora del Oporto - Manchester City en directo

Muuuuuy buenas tardeeeees. El Porto recibe en el Estádio do Dragão al Manchester City en un cruce que abre la jornada 1 de la fase de liga con mucho morbo sobre el césped. Dos clubes que ya conocen la gloria europea --los Dragões en 2004, los Citizens en 2023-- se citan en un escenario que además guarda un triste recuerdo para el City: allí perdieron la final de 2021 ante el Chelsea.

Farioli hace su estreno como técnico en la Champions al frente de un Porto que llega con siete victorias consecutivas en todas las competiciones, mientras que el City busca su cuarto triunfo seguido con Enzo Maresca en el banquillo. Aunque en Europa el do Dragão pesa: la temporada pasada estuvieron invictos en las seis eliminatorias de la Europa League disputadas en casa, hasta llegar a los cuartos de final. La preocupación llega arriba, con la baja de larga duración de Samu.

Enfrente, un City que llega con buenas sensaciones. En su último partido superó 1-0 al recién ascendido Coventry gracias a un cabezazo de Haaland, en el debut oficial de Enzo Fernández. Maresca tiene el equipo casi al completo, con Jérémy Doku como única baja por una lesión en el gemelo. Arriba, la referencia de siempre: Haaland lleva 34 goles en 39 partidos de Champions con el club, a solo dos del récord de Agüero.

Tenemos otro partidazo, tenemos otra noche preciosa, tenemos mucho que contar... así que no esperamos más, arrrrrrrrrancamooooooooos.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or: Sadio Mane and Achraf Hakimi nominated - but when will Africa win again?
articles.summary: Sadio Mane and Achraf Hakimi have been nominated for this year's Ballon d'Or - but when will an African claim football's top individual prize for the first time since 1995?
articles.body:
Africa has only ever had one Ballon d'Or winner, and the wait for someone to emulate George Weah is likely to be extended further after this year's nominations were revealed.

Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi and Senegal forward Sadio Mane are the continent's two names on the 30-strong list.

Both players have previously recorded top-six Ballon d'Or finishes but, after a year in which Spain lifted the Fifa World Cup and Kylian Mbappe netted 10 goals to become the tournament's all-time top scorer, the chances of the Paris St-Germain right-back or the Al-Nassr winger lifting the coveted trophy appear slim.

And it is not the first time that Africa has failed to make a big impact.

Part of the reason for the historic lack of success is down to the fact the award, which was first handed out by France Football magazine in 1956, was not open to players representing non-European nations until 1995.

That was the year that Liberian striker Weah scooped the prize after his impressive form for PSG and AC Milan.

Favourite Kane makes Ballon d'Or shortlist

Yet, for all the stars the continent has produced, the only other time an African player registered a top-three finish came in 2022, when Mane was second behind France striker Karim Benzema.

Of course, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have dominated proceedings for most of this century, scooping 13 of the 15 available Ballons d'Or between 2008 and 2023.

Journalists from the top 100 nations in the Fifa rankings will vote for the prize, with the recipient of the 2026 trophy announced at a ceremony in London on 26 October.

The "symbolic choice of venue" for the 70th anniversary of the award is in tribute to the inaugural winner, England winger Sir Stanley Matthews.

But how do the historic Ballon d'Or numbers stack up for Africa?

The high point of Africa's Ballon d'Or history clearly came in the very first year the continent's stars became eligible, with Weah topping the vote in 1995 ahead of Germany's Jurgen Klinsmann and Finland's Jari Litmanen.

Five more Africans made that year's 50-player list.

But only once since, in 2007, has the continent had as many as six nominations. On that occasion Didier Drogba was the highest-ranked finisher, with the Ivorian coming fourth.

The pool has narrowed since then, with 30 players in contention since 2008 and just 23 in the running when the Ballon d'Or was combined with the Fifa's world player of the year award between 2010 and 2015.

One other stand-out year for Africa came in 2019, when three men finished in the top 10. Mane came fourth, Egypt's Mohamed Salah was fifth, and Riyad Mahrez of Algeria tenth.

Which African nation has the most Ballon d'Or nominations?

In total, Africa has received 76 nominations for the Ballon d'Or since 1995.

That makes up just 6.62% of the overall hopefuls.

Cameroon legend Samuel Eto'o has the most nominations, having been in the running nine times in a row from 2003 to 2011. His best finish came in 2009 when he was fifth.

Drogba follows with eight nominations, with Salah on six.

Five-time nominee Mane has the greatest longevity of any African, with the 34-year-old's first and most recent appearances on the list coming 10 years apart.

Nigeria has had the most individual players listed for the award, with eight in total. Victor Osimhen's eighth-place finish in 2023 is the best performance by a Super Eagles player.

Thirty-nine African countries are still awaiting their first nominee, although Chad is surprisingly not among them after striker Japhet N'Doram was part of the 1995 list alongside Weah.

DR Congo and South Africa, ranked 43rd and 54th in the world respectively, are the highest-ranked nations still waiting to make the cut, while no player representing a club side on the continent has ever been nominated.

There have been nine years since 1995 when only one African was among the nominees.

The most recent of those instances was 2024, when Nigeria's Ademola Lookman finished 14th after scoring a hat-trick in the Europa League final for Atalanta.

African contenders have failed to pick up any votes on four occasions after being shortlisted: 1998 (Sunday Oliseh), 2000 (Geremi and Patrick Mboma), 2001 (Samuel Kuffour) and 2003 (Eto'o and Hatem Trabelsi).

Ballon d'Or nominations by African country

Ivory Coast - 15 (Didier Drogba 8, Yaya Toure 5, Kolo Toure, Sebastien Haller)

Cameroon - 12 (Samuel Eto'o 9, Geremi, Patrick Mboma, Andre Onana)

Nigeria - 10 (Jay-Jay Okocha 2, Nwankwo Kanu 2, Finidi George, Daniel Amokachi, Victor Ikpeba, Sunday Oliseh, Victor Osimhen, Ademola Lookman)

Senegal - 8 (Sadio Mane 5, Papa Bouba Diop, El Hadji Diouf, Kalidou Koulibaly)

Ghana - 6 (Michael Essien 3, Tony Yeboah, Samuel Kuffour, Asamoah Gyan)

Mali - 3 (Mahamadou Diarra 2, Frederic Kanoute)

Gabon - 3 (all Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang)

Morocco - 3 (Achraf Hakimi 2, Yassine Bounou)

Since the women's Ballon d'Or was first awarded in 2018, only four African players have been nominated.

Nigeria forward Asisat Oshoala was the first, making the 20- and 30-name shortlists in 2022 and 2023 respectively.

Zambia skipper Barbra Banda has been nominated in every year since, joined by Tabitha Chawinga of Malawi in 2024 and then her sister Temwa Chawinga in 2025 and 2026.

It means no more than two players from Africa have ever been listed for the prize in any one year.

The continent has had a total of 10 nominations from the 195 players nominated overall.

Ballon d'Or Feminin nominations by African country

Malawi - 3 (Temwa Chawinga 2, Tabitha Chawinga)

articles.title: A Belocian le sedujo la forma de jugar del Racing
articles.standfirst: "Tuve varias reuniones con el club y me convenció su estilo de juego"
articles.summary: "Tuve varias reuniones con el club y me convenció su estilo de juego"
articles.body: Jeanuël Belocian ha pasado por sala de prensa para ser presentado como nuevo jugador del Racing, después de disputar unos minutos en Butarque ante el Rayo Vallecano. El futbolista francés llegó al conjunto cántabro procedente del Bayer Leverkusen en calidad de cedido. Este próximo sábado ante el Alavés tiene muchas opciones de salir de inicio. Chema Aragón director deportivo del Racing reconocía la polivalencia de Belocian, ‘Puede jugar de central zurdo y de la lateral izquierdo. Es un futbolista de altísimo nivel y estoy encantado de que esté aquí. Tiene buen pie y capacidad para defender por alto’. El central francés también valoraba sus virtudes como futbolista, ‘Soy agresivo y me encanta tener balón’. Belocian apuntaba porque eligió al Racing, ‘ Este equipo es la mejor opción de las que tenía, aunque soy jugador del Bayer, quiero avanzar y este proyecto es el que más me convenía’. El nuevo futbolista encantado por dos motivos desde su llegada a Santander, ‘Quiero agradecer la acogida de mis nuevos compañeros, les doy las gracias y he venido aquí porque hay playa, soy de Guadalupe y para mi es muy importante’. Belocian se reía al hablar de la playa, pero reconocía su importancia en su vida cotidiana.

articles.title: El Assy desvela la estrategia del club para sobrevivir financieramente: vender, ahorrar y ascender
articles.standfirst: El director general del Almería anuncia alrededor de 27 millones de euros en pérdidas, pero no le impedirá fichar en enero
articles.summary: El director general del Almería anuncia alrededor de 27 millones de euros en pérdidas, pero no le impedirá fichar en enero
articles.body: Mohamed El Assy ha comparecido este mediodía para valorar el cierre de mercado de fichajes, aunque la comparecencia ha derivado más bien en un profundo análisis de la situación financiera del club. A pesar de anunciar un balance negativo momentáneo en las cuentas del club de alrededor de 27 millones de euros, ello no le impedirá fichar en el próximo mercado. Cabe destacar que el Almería no se encuentra en la famosa norma 1:1 en el límite salarial porque se encuentra sobrepasado. Tener unas cuentas con saldo positivo ayuda a tener un mayor límite salarial, pero no implica que no tengas posibilidad de fichar, sino que las normas para generar espacio salarial cambian y son más estrictas. El límite salarial nunca puede ser negativo puesto que va de cero a positivo. Carlos Martín: “La verdad que fue un poco molesto para nosotros no poder completar este fichaje. En los grandes clubes como el Atlético, muchos jugadores no quieren salir y después el último día tienen mucho trabajo porque finalmente muchos jugadores terminan saliendo. Tenían seis o siete operaciones por hacer y empezaron tarde el proceso con Carlos Martín. Perdimos el tiempo y al jugador, pero tenemos una plantilla muy competitiva y creemos que es suficiente para alcanzar los objetivos”. Reducción de gasto en fichajes: “Hablamos con la nueva dirección que debíamos cambiar la estrategia del club un poco. Creo que gastábamos demasiado y que podemos firmar muy buenos jugadores como estamos haciendo ahora sin gastar mucho. El club tiene muchos proyectos por hacer en temas de infraestructuras. Necesitamos tener dinero para completar la Fase 2 del estadio y el próximo año llevar a cabo la ciudad deportiva. Tenemos que seguir con las ventas que estamos realizando. Desde que llegué aquí con mi equipo nos hemos situado como el octavo equipo en España con mayor beneficio por venta de jugadores. Estamos muy contentos con esta nueva política de fichajes que permite reducir gasto”. Margen salarial de cara al mercado invernal: “Anunciaremos el presupuesto pronto puesto que estamos cerrando algunos contratos con ‘sponsors’. Con respecto al límite salarial, tenemos margen para firmar dos jugadores o más en enero. Creo que disponemos de un millón y medio o quizás un poco más para firmar jugadores”. Ciudad deportiva: “Estamos esperando a que el Ayuntamiento nos de la licencia, creemos que en enero. Estamos preparados financieramente para empezar con las obras directamente en cuanto tengamos los permisos”. Mercado de agentes libres: “Para mí traer un jugador como, por ejemplo, Rodrigo Ely, es más importante que traer un gran nombre que no sea leal al proyecto, que nunca haya jugado aquí o que no tenga la motivación de ayudarnos. Prefiero eso a traer a una gran estrella en el final de su carrera porque en muchos casos esa no es la mejor decisión y no es la manera en la que hacemos las cosas aquí en Almería. Aquí creamos estrellas”. Ventas: “Hemos sacado alrededor de 25 millones de euros en ventas. De los jugadores más valiosos solo hemos vendido a Lopy y hemos conseguido retener a Arribas, Dzodic, Chirino o Bonini, que tuvieron varias ofertas”. Situación económica: “Con el sistema de derechos televisivos, es muy complicado sobrevivir para los equipos que descienden en caso de no regresar a Primera de manera inmediata. El primer año tienes el paracaídas de la ayuda de LaLiga, pero si te mantienes tres años en Segunda es muy complicado. Por eso veis muchos equipos que descienden a Primera RFEF. Por suerte, nosotros tenemos esa estrategia de venta de grandes jugadores y ‘sponsors’ que nos ha ayudado a sobrevivir. Creo que los equipos que descienden a Segunda deberían tener una ayuda de LaLiga, al menos, durante tres temporadas. Nosotros tenemos unas pérdidas alrededor de 27 millones de euros”. Arribas: “No ha sido uno de los mercados veraniegos más fuertes de los últimos años a nivel general. Arribas tuvo el interés de varios equipos, pero ninguno se decidió por diferentes razones. Algunos porque para firmar debían vender antes y no lo lograron o situaciones así. Nosotros siempre acordamos con los jugadores el valor que vamos a pedir por ellos. Estamos muy contentos de que Arribas se haya quedado. Estamos preparados para sobrevivir financieramente sin tener que vender a Arribas, no hay ningún problema. En caso de que esa cantidad en la que lo hemos evaluado llegue en enero o cuando sea, nosotros ayudaremos al jugador a salir. En ese caso, estaríamos preparados para competir y ganar sin Arribas”. Rubi: “El contrato de Rubi era de dos años más uno opcional. Este último era obligado en caso de que el Almería estuviera en Primera División. Sin el ascenso, pasó a ser únicamente de dos temporadas”. Ayudas económicas del propietario: “Mohamed Al Khereiji nos facilitó un préstamo el año pasado (30 millones) y este año nos ha ayudado también con una pequeña cantidad en concepto de préstamo. Esta es una de las explicaciones de por qué ese cambio de estrategia en el mercado, pero necesitamos ascender. Al final esa será la solución. Con el ascenso, con la estrategia de ventas, con unos accionistas fuertes que nos apoyan, también con el aspecto comercial que estamos mejorando, además de los nuevos ingresos de la segunda fase del estadio a largo plazo, os aseguro que solventaremos el tema financiero. Pero necesitamos ascender. Debemos esperar hasta enero para ver si necesitamos que el presidente nos ayude económicamente o somos autosuficientes. Siempre hablamos del presidente, pero al final son diferentes miembros del consejo los que tienen acciones del club y todos ellos tienen una muy buena situación financiera personal”.

articles.title: Dabo Swinney Rips Reporter on Video For Question on Roster After Clemson's Blowout Loss to LSU
articles.summary: Clemson football started the season with a 51-10 road loss to LSU on Saturday.
articles.body:
Clemson football started the season with a 51-10 road loss to LSU on Saturday.

On Tuesday, Chapel Fowler of The State asked Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney whether he regretted any decisions regarding his offseason roster construction. Swinney provided the following response.

Report Card Grades for CFB's Top QBs 🧑‍🏫

"No, I don't," Swinney said in part. "I don't man. I regret being 0-1 right now. I regret that. But no. Can you ask me that at the end of the season? The season ain't over. I mean, we got one game. We got 11 more. What if we go 11-1? You promise me you'll ask that then? OK, good, I'll answer that."

Swinney kept elaborating on the matter, noting how the season is just one week old (h/t Tony Crumpton of TigerNet).

"We've played one game. Did you play football? Okay, well, they give you 12 games, and at the end of the year, you count them up. That's when those types of questions are fair to me, not after one game to maybe the best team in the country.

"Other people have good teams and coaches and things like that, too. So I give them credit. We've got 11 more games to go battle. We'll count them up. Then you can ask me whatever question you want."

You can look at that interaction two ways.

On one hand, Swinney is right. It is only one week into the season, and Clemson could get it together and finish strong. The Tigers play only one more ranked opponent (albeit a tough one, No. 7 Miami at home on Oct. 3), but they could be playing for a College Football Playoff berth in December in the ACC Championship Game. The season certainly is not over.

On the other hand, Clemson suffered a brutal defeat. After an early Clemson field goal, LSU scored 51 unanswered points before the visitors scored a garbage-time touchdown to help get into double-digit scoring. LSU out-gained Clemson 644-145, including 335 yards passing and 309 yards rushing. The Tigers also had 38 first downs to Clemson's eight.

The Lane Kiffin-led LSU team, powered by 44 transfers , could very well be a national powerhouse now. Still, Clemson could not compete with LSU, and it's fair to wonder whether this roster might be in for a tough 2026.

That said, Clemson has a chance to rewrite the narrative week by week. A home date with Georgia Southern looms Saturday, and then the ACC slate begins on Saturday, Sept. 19 when the Tigers welcome Bill Belichick's UNC squad to Clemson.

articles.title: Iowa Band Member Derek Phillips Dies After Collapsing at Week 1 Game
articles.summary: University of Iowa band member Derek Phillips died Tuesday morning after collapsing during Saturday's season-opening football game between the Hawkeyes and Northern Illinois.
articles.body:
University of Iowa band member Derek Phillips died Tuesday morning after collapsing during Saturday's season-opening football game between the Hawkeyes and Northern Illinois.

The school announced the news in a statement.

In a post on his Instagram written by his family Tuesday morning, they said they made the "heartbreaking decision to remove" Phillips from life support after he suffered "sudden cardiac arrest" during the game:

Sark 'Shocked' by Michigan Field Storming

"Despite the extraordinary efforts of the ICU team at the University of Iowa Hospital, the damage to his brain was too severe, and we have made the heartbreaking decision to remove life support. ... Derek is comfortable, surrounded by family, and enveloped in the music he loved so much. Thank you for every prayer, every shared experience, and every bit of love you've given to our boy."

University of Iowa Public Relations Manager Chris Brewer issued a statement about Phillips to Evan Watson of the Daily Iowan :

"The entire Hawkeye Marching Band family is thinking of Derek Phillips and his loved ones. We are grateful to his parents for providing regular updates to the students who love Derek. This is heartbreaking for everyone who cares for him. The university is in close contact and is offering support."

Iowa announced during the game that the marching band was foregoing the scheduled halftime performance due to the heat.

Phillips was a third-year student at the University of Iowa.

"Derek Phillips was our mellophone section leader, a beloved member of the School of Music horn studio, and the kind of friend, student, and musician that represents the very best of what it means to be a Hawkeye," the band program wrote in its statement.

articles.title: AP College Football Poll 2026 Week 2 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: Despite no major upsets in the first full week of the 2026 college football season, the top of the Associated Press Top 25 poll has shifted based on some of the results.
articles.body:
Despite no major upsets in the first full week of the 2026 college football season, the top of the A ssociated Press Top 25 poll has shifted based on some of the results.

Ohio State remains atop the rankings after an easy 56-3 win over Ball State, but Oregon's close call against Boise State knocked it down four spots after being No. 2 in the preseason poll.

Report Card Grades for CFB's Top QBs 🧑‍🏫

Oregon had the most interesting result from Week 1 after trailing by as many as 10 points at home against Boise State. The Ducks survived 34-27 thanks to Dante Moore's 378 yards passing and three touchdowns.

Boise State is a better opponent than most teams at the top of the rankings went up against to start the season, but an Oregon loss right out of the gate could have immediately derailed things for a team that most analysts believe is one of the top title contenders in the nation.

The team that moved into Oregon's spot at No. 2 is Georgia coming off an easy 63-3 win over Tennessee State.

Notre Dame, which had one of the best performances of any team in the country all weekend, jumped up one spot in the rankings to No. 3.

Playing what was technically neutral-site game against Wisconsin at Lambeau Field, the Fighting Irish dropped 28 points in the second half en route to a 41-13 victory.

Other than Oregon, the only real close call for a top-10 team was Ole Miss against a Louisville team that was ranked No. 24 in the preseason poll. Mississippi won 41-38 on Lucas Carneiro's 48-yard field goal as time expired.

Despite the loss, Louisville maintained its same spot in the rankings coming off a strong showing on the road against a high-level opponent.

Lane Kiffin kicked off his tenure at LSU with an impressive 51-10 win over Clemson in what was the largest margin of defeat of Dabo Swinney's career with the program.

Michigan, on the heels of a controversial win over Western Michigan, fell outside of the top 25 after being ranked No. 16 in the preseason poll.

Looking ahead to Week 2, the marquee matchup is arguably the biggest regular-season game of the season between No. 1 Ohio State and No. 4 Texas. The Buckeyes won 14-7 in the season opener for both teams last year at the Horseshoe.

Saturday's showdown between the Buckeyes and Longhorns will be played in Austin. No. 11 Oklahoma at Michigan is the other big game on the schedule.

articles.title: El plan de regeneración económica del Sevilla
articles.standfirst: En tres temporadas, los hispalenses han recortado 121 millones en masa salarial, han reducido la deuda neta a 60 millones y rozan el equilibrio financiero
articles.summary: En tres temporadas, los hispalenses han recortado 121 millones en masa salarial, han reducido la deuda neta a 60 millones y rozan el equilibrio financiero
articles.body: El Sevilla ha dado otro paso hacia adelante dentro de la reestructuración financiera más drástica de su historia reciente. El drama que supuso el cierre del ejercicio 2023-24, con un déficit de hasta 82 millones de euros tras su última participación en la Liga de Campeones, obligó a que la entidad redefiniera su modelo de gestión. Para garantizar su viabilidad a largo plazo y evitar una brecha insalvable, la cúpula hispalense cambió de rumbo radicalmente, enfocándose en soltar el lastre de unos costes sobredimensionados sin los ingresos recurrentes de las competiciones europeas. Tres años más tarde, el plan de regeneración económica diseñado para sanear las arcas del Sevilla comienza a dar sus primeros frutos. Una vez que se ha cerrado el mercado estival, los números ofrecidos demuestran que la transición hacia este contexto de austeridad no solo ha evitado el colapso de la sociedad, sino que le ha devuelto mayor sostenibilidad. Un viraje que permite atajar las pérdidas y, al fin, sentar los cimientos de una estructura financiera equilibrada. El dato más revelador de este volantazo estratégico se observa en la masa salarial del primer equipo. En la temporada 2023-24, el gasto en plantilla ascendía a unos inasumibles 193 millones de euros entre sueldos y amortizaciones. Dos años y medio después, en esta campaña 2026-27 la partida económica destinada se ha reducido a 72 millones de euros. Es decir, el club se ahorra el 62,6% (121 millones de euros) adaptando los sueldos a su realidad actual, donde muy pocos futbolistas superan los dos millones de euros brutos anuales. "Hemos estado dos temporadas donde hemos sufrido mucho en lo deportivo y teníamos que buscar plantillas más eficientes donde todo el dinero que gastemos tenga la camiseta del Sevilla y juegue en el Sevilla", explicaba el presidente José María del Nido Carrasco durante la comparecencia de este martes. La nueva escala salarial es la piedra angular del proyecto de José Ignacio Navarro en la dirección deportiva. Paradójicamente, el reajuste deja un equipo que, después de lo visto en este arranque de Liga, transmite mejores sensaciones que en cursos anteriores. La contención del gasto ha sido integral en todas las áreas del Sevilla. Los gastos operativos no deportivos han pasado de 61 millones de euros en el último año de Champions League a 48 millones en la presente campaña, lo que representa un recorte de 13 millones. Esta disciplina financiera ha permitido estrechar el déficit de forma paulatina durante estos tres años: tras los -82 millones de la 2023-24 y los -54 millones de la 2024-25, la sangría se redujo a -27 millones en la 2025-26. Para esta temporada, las previsiones en el Sevilla contemplan un desfase de apenas -4 millones de euros. Este balance incluso podría convertirse en positivo si se cristalizara la salida de Fábio Cardoso -aún le buscan acomodo en los mercados que siguen abiertos-, la firma del patrocinador principal o la venta de algún otro futbolista en la ventana de invierno. En el caso de lograrlo, el club cerraría un ejercicio en números verdes por primera vez desde antes de la pandemia. El otro gran frente abierto del Sevilla es el pasivo circulante y la deuda con entidades financieras, que se sitúa en 90 millones de euros. Sin embargo, los movimientos del mercado veraniego han ayudado a reducir ese agujero en 30 millones en menos de un trimestre, fijando la deuda neta actual en 60 millones de euros. Según explicó Del Nido Carrasco, esta reducción del pasivo permitiría atender con normalidad el pago de los créditos solicitados en años anteriores, alejando cualquier fantasma de quiebra técnica o problemas de liquidez a medio plazo. "Cuando tomé posesión del cargo uno de los objetivos prioritarios era cuadrar cuentas. En los últimos 24 meses hemos reducido los gastos de 265 a 135 millones de euros", manifestó el presidente del Sevilla. Con la deuda neta estabilizada y un coste de plantilla proporcional a los ingresos, en Nervión están cerca de volver a equilibrar las cuentas. Ahora miran hacia el futuro con la certeza de que el proyecto deportivo se cimenta de nuevo sobre tierra firme.

articles.title: MAC Files Appeal with NCAA over WMU's Loss to Michigan, Says Replay Protocol Wasn't Followed
articles.summary: Another layer was added to the controversy surrounding Michigan's last-second win over Western Michigan in Saturday night's season opener.
articles.body:
Another layer was added to the controversy surrounding Michigan's last-second win over Western Michigan in Saturday night's season opener.

The MAC filed a formal appeal with the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee on Tuesday, asserting that "replay protocol was not properly followed" at the end of Saturday's game and requesting that Western Michigan be recognized as the winner.

Big Ten Addresses Controversial Clock Ruling

The Wolverines entered the year ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25, but they needed some extra help to avoid a major upset against the Broncos.

After Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary pass sailed out of bounds as time expired, one second was put back on the clock following a disputed replay decision. Underwood's second Hail Mary attempt was caught by JJ Buchanan for a 47-yard touchdown to give Michigan a 13-12 victory. Despite the win, the Wolverines were knocked out of the Top 25.

The Big Ten stood by the controversial replay review in a statement released two hours after the game.

"It was determined Western Michigan No. 18 started his jump from an established out-of-bounds position [left foot] and made contact with the ball with one second remaining on the clock," the statement said, citing the rule that stops the clock on such contact.

Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna told ESPN's Jake Trotter that the Big Ten's replay review process isn't "as good as it could be."

"And that's because what the [TV] viewers see in a pivotal question is different than what the review process shows," Kavalhuna said. "Is there a real reason why we can't have those things equal? And if there is, let's try and fix that. And if there isn't a real reason why we can't have those things synced up, then we should sync them up so that everybody who's watching at home doesn't start to wonder what happened."

It now appears that the MAC isn't willing to go down without fighting to rectify the situation for the Broncos. Western Michigan will try to bounce back against Monmouth on Saturday, while Michigan will face a tough test against No. 11 Oklahoma.

articles.title: Deion Sanders' Colorado Gains 1st AP Votes for 2026 After Dramatic Win vs. Georgia Tech
articles.summary: After Colorado secured a gutsy win over Georgia Tech to start its season, a few voters believe the Buffaloes should be in the AP Top 25.
articles.body:
After Colorado secured a gutsy win over Georgia Tech to start its season, a few voters believe the Buffaloes should be in the AP Top 25.

Deion Sanders' Buffaloes earned three votes in the first AP Poll of the season, though it wasn't enough for them to crack the top-25 following the close win over the Yellow Jackets.

Georgia Tech led the Buffaloes 10-7 heading into the final quarter of Thursday's game, and Colorado had the chance to tie it with a field goal early in the fourth, but the attempt was blocked.

Report Card Grades for CFB's Top QBs 🧑‍🏫

The Yellow Jackets then made a field goal to go up 13-7 with just under two minutes to play. Colorado quarterback Julian Lewis executed a tremendous 75-yard drive that ended with a Buffaloes touchdown.

But Colorado still needed a stop, and Georgia Tech put some pressure on Sanders' defense when it got into field goal range. Boo Carter played the hero for the Buffs, though, blocking the Yellow Jackets' game-winning field goal attempt from 45 yards.

While Colorado and Georgia Tech delivered an instant classic to start the season, the Buffaloes clearly have some work to do, mainly on offense.

Lewis finished with just 124 passing yards and a touchdown on 14-of-27 passing as Colorado struggled to get much going through the air. Sanders will get the chance to make some tune-ups as it faces Weber State on Saturday.

It's hard to judge just how impressive the win was given that it was the first game of the season, but the next week of action could be telling. Georgia Tech will face a top-20 Tennessee team on Saturday, and a win over the Vols would make Colorado's win last week look even more impressive.

Regardless, the win over the Yellow Jackets is a step in the right direction for Colorado. The Buffaloes beat just one Power 4 team last season, and they've already matched that after Week 1.

articles.title: Michigan Drops Out of AP Poll Top 25 After Controversial Hail Mary Win, WMU Gains Votes
articles.summary: Michigan's controversial victory over Western Michigan on Saturday, after they were given one last second on the clock and another chance at a Hail Mary, wasn't devoid of repercussions.
articles.body:
Michigan's controversial victory over Western Michigan on Saturday, after they were given one last second on the clock and another chance at a Hail Mary, wasn't devoid of repercussions.

The Wolverines were ranked No. 16 in the Associated Press' preseason poll but were dropped out of the top 25 entirely in the Week 1 rankings . Western Michigan, meanwhile, picked up 12 votes.

The Wolverines still received 69 votes and remain on the cusp of the top 25.

It appeared that Michigan had suffered a stunning 12-7 loss against Western Michigan, at home, after Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary attempt sailed out of bounds with the stadium and broadcast clock hitting zero. But Big Ten replay officials reviewed the play and determined that WMU safety Micah Davis had jumped from out of bounds and touched the ball before the clock hit zero, giving Michigan one more second—and one last Hail Mary attempt.

This time, Underwood connected with JJ Buchanan on a 47-yard touchdown heave, giving Michigan a 13-12 win and creating some early controversy for the 2026 college football season.

Big Ten officials issued the following statement after the game:

Mid-American Conference officials initially accepted that reasoning and ruling, as did Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna.

"It is just a discrepancy," he said in a press conference after the game. "What the viewing public see and what the reviewing officials see are different. I used to be a federal prosecutor. I've looked into this pretty closely, and I don't discern anything unfair or untoward in this process."

But on Monday, the MAC said in a statement that the replay protocols were incorrectly applied and the conference formally appealed the result, hoping to overturn Michigan's controversial win:

AP voters, meanwhile, already issued their own ruling on the matter, dropping Michigan out of the top 25 entirely.

As for the rest of the poll, Ohio State remained the No. 1 team, while Georgia moved up one spot to No. 2, Notre Dame moved up a spot to No. 3, Texas moved up one spot to No. 4 and Indiana moved up one spot to No. 5.

Oregon, following a close call against Boise State, dropped four spots to No. 6. LSU moved up three spots to No. 8 following its blowout of Clemson, while Virginia moved up 21 spots to No. 25 despite having a bye week (the Cavaliers did beat NC State 34-8 on Aug. 29, however).

articles.title: El Aston Villa se quita el tapón y estrena la Champions a lo grande
articles.standfirst: Los de Emery consiguen su primera victoria de la temporada en una exhibición de los jugadores de ataque ante un Brujas que tuvo en el español Virgili a su mejor jugador
articles.summary: Los de Emery consiguen su primera victoria de la temporada en una exhibición de los jugadores de ataque ante un Brujas que tuvo en el español Virgili a su mejor jugador
articles.body: La espera se terminó y la Champions League volvió a entrar en escena. La nueva temporada de la mejor competición de clubes se estrenó con un partido que no defraudó para nada. Brujas y Aston Villa disputaron un encuentro con muchísimas ocasiones y en el que los ataques se impusieron claramente a las defensas. Llegaban los de Unai Emery a este compromiso tras un inicio complicado. Los villanos no conocían la victoria en los primeros cuatro partidos de la temporada, pero llegó la Champions League y sacaron su mejor versión. Desde el inicio del partido dejaron clara su intención de atacar y sólo tardaron 11 minutos en adelantarse a través de McGinn. El incombustible capitán escocés mandó a guardar el balón con un gran tiro ajustado desde la derecha. En los mejores minutos de los ingleses consiguió reaccionar el Brujas, a través de Jan Virgili. El extremo fue un dolor de cabeza para Wan-Bissaka, y el centro atrás del español lo empujó Vetlsen al fondo de la red para empatar el partido. Pero inmediatamente después se cambiaron los papeles; cuando más apretaban los belgas Buendía silenció el Jan Breydel sólo tres minutos después. A partir de ahí, una sucesión de ocasiones que hicieron trabajar a Sommer y Suzuki. Sin embargo, el buen trabajo del portero suizo que había evitado algún gol se vio empañado con el error que llevó al tercer gol del Aston Villa. Justo antes del descanso, un balón largo de Pau Torres hacia Nicolas Jackson provocó la salida hasta casi el centro del campo de Sommer, que vio como el rápido delantero senegalés se le adelantó para marcar a placer. Era difícil mantener el ritmo que impusieron ambos equipos durante los 90 minutos, y se notó en el segundo tiempo. Después de un cuarto de hora con pocas oportunidades, una mano sin discusión de Wan-Bissaka permitió a Tresoldi recortar distancias de penalti. El Brujas apretó los siguientes minutos pero Unai Emery consiguió con los cambios frenar el arreón de los locales. El conjunto inglés apenas sufrió en los instantes finales y consiguió cerrar el triunfo. Importante victoria de los villanos, que consiguen los tres primeros puntos de la Champions League para quitarse las malas sensaciones en el arranque de la Premier y empezar a asentar las bases de este nuevo proyecto que ha sufrido una clara reconstrucción.

articles.title: Quién es Michael Oliver, árbitro del Real Madrid - Inter de hoy en Champions League
articles.standfirst: El colegiado inglés dirigirá por sexta vez al Real Madrid en Europa en el estreno de Champions ante el Inter (martes, 21:00 h)
articles.summary: El colegiado inglés dirigirá por sexta vez al Real Madrid en Europa en el estreno de Champions ante el Inter (martes, 21:00 h)
articles.body: Michael Oliver será el árbitro del Real Madrid-Inter de Milán, correspondiente a la primera jornada de la Champions League, que se disputará en el Santiago Bernabéu el martes a las 21:00 horas. El colegiado inglés, uno de los más reputados del continente, dirigirá por sexta vez al conjunto blanco en competición europea, un historial que deja un balance netamente favorable para los madridistas. Y es que, de los cinco precedentes anteriores, el Madrid solo conoció la derrota en una ocasión. Oliver arbitró el Real Madrid-Eintracht de la Supercopa de Europa 2022 (2-0), el Braga-Real Madrid de la fase de grupos de la 2023/24 (1-2), el Olympiacos-Real Madrid de la pasada edición (3-4) y, ya con signo adverso, el Real Madrid-Bayern de los cuartos de la 2025/26 (1-2). Un bagaje de cuatro victorias y una sola derrota bajo su silbato. Pero si hay un partido que ha ligado para siempre el nombre de Oliver a la historia reciente del Madrid, ese es el Real Madrid-Juventus de los cuartos de final de la Champions 2017/18. Aquella noche, con el Bernabéu al borde de la prórroga y la eliminatoria en el alambre tras el 3-0 de la 'Vecchia Signora', el inglés señaló un penalti de Benatia sobre Lucas Vázquez en el minuto 93 que desató la tormenta. Cristiano Ronaldo transformó la pena máxima y clasificó al Madrid para las semifinales. La decisión provocó la airada reacción de la Juventus, con un Gianluigi Buffon que se abalanzó sobre el colegiado hasta ser expulsado, y que después cargó duramente contra él en zona mixta. El episodio, que le valió al portero una sanción de la UEFA, convirtió a Oliver en objeto de una campaña de acoso que el propio organismo condenó y que llegó a salpicar a su familia. Un capítulo tan polémico como inolvidable. El conjunto nerazzurro, viejo conocido del Madrid en Europa, se cruzará así con un árbitro que ya sabe lo que es dirigir citas de máxima tensión en el coliseo blanco. El martes, con el estreno continental en juego, Oliver vuelve a un escenario que conoce bien.

articles.body: El colegiado italiano Simone Sozza ha sido designado para dirigir partidos decisivos en el arranque del torneo continental. Su amplia trayectoria en la Serie A avala su capacidad directiva. Sozza comenzó su carrera arbitral en 2004 a los diecisiete años en la sección de Seregno. Tras ascender progresivamente por las categorías regionales y la Serie D, logró consolidarse en el fútbol profesional italiano con excelentes actuaciones técnicas que llamaron la atención de los comités de arbitraje. Su debut en la Serie A se produjo a principios de 2020 durante un encuentro entre el Parma y el Udinese. Desde entonces, el colegiado lombardo ha dirigido grandes clásicos del fútbol transalpino, incluyendo derbis de gran tensión en Milán, Turín y la capital italiana. En 2023 ingresó oficialmente en la nómina de árbitros internacionales de la FIFA, hito histórico para su sección local. A partir de esa fecha ha dirigido encuentros decisivos en torneos de selecciones absolutas, eliminatorias sudamericanas de formación y choques clave de la Liga de Campeones. Su gran labor técnica le valió la promoción a la categoría First de la UEFA en 2024. Galardonado con prestigiosos premios individuales por su rigurosidad en el campo, el juez italiano garantiza un arbitraje de máxima garantías para los duelos más exigentes de Europa.

A pesar de haber traspasado a futbolistas clave como Bouaddi o Fernández-Pardo, el equipo mantiene una propuesta futbolística dinámica, competitiva e invicta en este inicio de temporada. La gran referencia ofensiva del equipo galo es el veterano delantero Olivier Giroud, especialista en fijar centrales y rematar balones al área. Además, la plantilla cuenta con el exbético Romain Perraud en banda, aportando profundidad y conocimiento táctico sobre el estilo de juego del conjunto verdiblanco. Davide Ancelotti ha implantado una idea de juego basada en la posesión inteligente y el repliegue coordinado. El Lille sabe juntar sus líneas cuando no tiene el balón, para posteriormente iniciar ataques organizados buscando la envergadura de sus atacantes. Su equilibrio defensivo es su mayor virtud actual. El Betis se encontrará con un adversario muy disciplinado que apenas concede espacios entre líneas. La fortaleza como local del conjunto francés pondrá a prueba el regreso verdiblanco a la élite europea. El duelo táctico en el centro del campo definirá las opciones de ambos contendientes.

articles.title: MAC says replay mistake handed Michigan another play, pushes to erase controversial win
articles.summary: The Mid-American Conference announced it had submitted formal appeals to recognize Western Michigan University as the winners of Saturday’s controversial game.
articles.body: The Mid-American Conference announced it had submitted formal appeals on Tuesday to recognize Western Michigan University as the winners of Saturday’s game against Michigan, which was won on a controversial last-second play. The Wolverines defeated the Broncos 13-12 on a final-play Hail Mary pass from Bryce Underwood to JJ Buchanan – a play that many believe shouldn’t have happened. A play before, the clock appeared to run out as Underwood hurled a long pass to the end zone that fell to the field incomplete. A replay review by officials determined there was one second left, despite replays showing the clock appeared to have hit :00 before the play was over. The Big Ten provided an explanation for the call, stating that a clock that was not seen on TV or in the stadium was the official clock and that reading was used to allow the final play. On Tuesday, MAC commissioner Dr. Jon Steinbrecher said the Big Ten had violated replay protocols and WMU should have been declared the winner. “After further study and investigation, it is now evident that replay protocol was not properly followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock at the conclusion of the Western Michigan vs. Michigan football game,” Steinbrecher wrote in a statement. “The established replay protocol requires that the game clock displayed on the program feed be used in determining whether time remained. Instead, the Big Ten Conference replay crew relied upon the clock feed embedded within its replay system. As a result, one second was placed back on the game clock and an additional play was awarded. “This was not a judgment regarding the proper amount of time to place on the clock. It was an error in the application of the established replay protocol governing this specific end-of-game timing situation. Had the protocol been properly followed and the program-feed clock been used, no additional play would have been awarded, and Western Michigan would have won the game, 12–7.” Steinbrecher wrote that the MAC is asking the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff recognize the Broncos as the official winner of the game “for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations, and take such other corrective action as may be within their authority.” In a letter to the NCAA, the MAC was clear that the review itself was appropriate. “The issue before the Committee is not whether replay review was appropriate. It was. The issue is how the replay review was conducted and whether the established protocol governing an end-of-half timing situation was followed. It was not,” the letter states. The final moments of the game have been replayed and analyzed as much as any in recent memory. With nine seconds to play, Underwood dropped back to pass, scrambled and heaved a last-ditch pass that sailed out of bounds. The clocks on the scoreboard available to viewers at home and those in the stadium appeared to show zero when the ball hit a WMU defender’s hands. Officials called for a review and spent a long time looking at the play. They eventually decided that the official clock – which was different than the TV clock and the stadium clock – showed there was one second left in regulation. According to the MAC’s letter to the NCAA, the established protocol for what was supposed to happen in a replay review was not followed. “Rather than relying upon the designated game clock displayed on the program feed, the Big Ten replay crew relied upon a separate clock embedded within its replay system. The two clock feeds were not synchronized,” the letter states. “The game clock displayed on the program feed showed that the clock had expired. The clock embedded within the replay system, however, showed time remaining. Despite the protocol expressly requiring replay officials to rely solely upon the game clock displayed on the program feed, the replay crew utilized the unsynchronized replay-system clock and restored time to the game clock.” That extra second allowed for one more play to be called. Underwood’s second heaved prayer resulted in a touchdown, handing Michigan an unlikely win. In the overnight hours after the game, the Big Ten released an explanation and video, revealing the existence of the unseen clock. Western Michigan and the MAC initially said they accepted what transpired and took the high road in postgame comments. The victory didn’t help Michigan keep its place in the AP rankings released on Tuesday. The Wolverines slipped out of the Top 25 poll and face a matchup against No. 11 Oklahoma on Saturday. This story has been updated with additional reporting.

articles.title: MAC now says Big Ten replay officials erred in adding 1 second back for Michigan's Hail Mary, asks NCAA to recognize Western Michigan as the winner
articles.summary: The MAC says that replay officials didn't properly follow protocol.
articles.body:
The controversy surrounding Michigan's win over Western Michigan is far from over.

After initially accepting the Big Ten's explanation for how one second was added back to the clock for the Wolverines to throw a Hail Mary in their 13-12 win over the Broncos , the Mid-American Conference issued a statement Tuesday saying that replay protocols were actually not followed and Western Michigan should have won the game.

"After further study and investigation, it is now evident that replay protocol was not properly followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock at the conclusion of the Western Michigan vs. Michigan football game," the statement said. "The established replay protocol requires that the game clock displayed on the program feed be used in determining whether time remained. Instead, the Big Ten Conference replay crew relied upon the clock feed embedded within its replay system. As a result, one second was placed back on the game clock and an additional play was awarded. "This was not a judgment regarding the proper amount of time to place on the clock. It was an error in the application of the established replay protocol governing this specific end-of-game timing situation. Had the protocol been properly followed and the program-feed clock been used, no additional play would have been awarded and Western Michigan would have won the game, 12-7. "As a result, the Mid-American Conference has submitted formal appeals to the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff. The MAC is requesting that those bodies recognize Western Michigan as the actual winner of the game for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations and take such other corrective action as may be within their authority."

Instead, the Big Ten Conference replay crew relied upon the clock feed embedded within its replay system. As a result, one second was placed back on the game clock and an additional play was awarded.

"This was not a judgment regarding the proper amount of time to place on the clock. It was an error in the application of the established replay protocol governing this specific end-of-game timing situation. Had the protocol been properly followed and the program-feed clock been used, no additional play would have been awarded and Western Michigan would have won the game, 12-7.

"As a result, the Mid-American Conference has submitted formal appeals to the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff. The MAC is requesting that those bodies recognize Western Michigan as the actual winner of the game for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations and take such other corrective action as may be within their authority."

Michigan's initial Hail Mary attempt fell incomplete with seemingly no time remaining before officials added a second back to the game clock after determining that WMU Micah Davis touched the ball — after he leaped from out of bounds — before time expired.

In the formal appeal to the FBS oversight committee, MAC commissioner Jon Steinbrecher says the "established protocol" for replay reviews is for the in-stadium game clock to be inserted on the program feed and that "the replay official/replay center official then determines whether time should be restored to the game clock based solely upon the game clock insert on the program feed."

The game clock that was inserted into NBC's replays showed the clock at 0:00 when Davis touched the football. In its explanation hours after the game was over , the Big Ten showed that there was one second remaining on the clock its replay center had a camera trained on throughout the game.

"Rather than relying upon the designated game clock displayed on the program feed, the Big Ten replay crew relied upon a separate clock embedded within its replay system. The two clock feeds were not synchronized," the MAC wrote. "The game clock displayed on the program feed showed that the clock had expired. The clock embedded within the replay system, however, showed time remaining. Despite the protocol expressly requiring replay officials to rely solely upon the game clock displayed on the program feed, the replay crew utilized the unsynchronized replay-system clock and restored time to the game clock."

"Rather than relying upon the designated game clock displayed on the program feed, the Big Ten replay crew relied upon a separate clock embedded within its replay system. The two clock feeds were not synchronized," the MAC wrote.

"The game clock displayed on the program feed showed that the clock had expired. The clock embedded within the replay system, however, showed time remaining. Despite the protocol expressly requiring replay officials to rely solely upon the game clock displayed on the program feed, the replay crew utilized the unsynchronized replay-system clock and restored time to the game clock."

The MAC goes on to say that "the outcome of this game was not changed by a discretionary judgment made within the rules" but rather "it was changed because the established procedure for determining whether time remained on the game clock was not followed, and an unsynchronized clock was used in place of the clock specifically designated by the governing replay protocol."

The conference's appeal comes two days after Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna and coach Lance Taylor held a news conference to say that they accepted the Big Ten's explanation for how the decision was made to add a second back to the clock.

"I would say what the viewing public see and the officials see are different," Kavalhuna said Sunday. "And that's clear. I will say, I've looked into this pretty closely and I used to be a federal prosecutor — I don't discern anything unfair or untoward in this process. Can the process be improved by having what the viewing public see as what the reviewing officials see? Maybe. Frankly, that's not for me to decide."

After the MAC's statement Tuesday, Kavalhuna said that what the conference had done was "important action."

"Commissioner Steinbrecher and the MAC have taken important action today in college football," Kavalhuna's statement said. "The support we have received from across the country for Coach Taylor and our Broncos, for their character and their sportsmanship, has been overwhelming, and we are grateful for it. "Some have read our actions as weak. However, supporting student-athletes and their growth during a time of adversity is a strength. Being bitter doesn't make you better and this should not be mistaken for weakness or agreement. We can show respect for the game while also asking serious questions; I've done both and I'll keep doing both. Our job at Western Michigan is to play the game and help our students grow. It's the job of the conferences and the NCAA to enforce the rules. Our Broncos will continue to take the field against any opponent."

Being bitter doesn't make you better and this should not be mistaken for weakness or agreement. We can show respect for the game while also asking serious questions; I've done both and I'll keep doing both. Our job at Western Michigan is to play the game and help our students grow. It's the job of the conferences and the NCAA to enforce the rules. Our Broncos will continue to take the field against any opponent."

NBC said in a statement at halftime of Sunday's game between Washington and Washington State that its cameras "are not the official arbiter" of game time and that keeping track of the game clock was the responsibility of the Big Ten and its officials. NBC's clock appeared to have potentially started early ahead of the final snap of the game, though that was impossible to figure out for numerous reasons.

College football game clocks do not show fractions of a second and, to date, the Big Ten has not released a full video of the play side-by-side with its official game clock. The video the conference provided late Saturday night only showed the end of the play when players were crowded in the end zone attempting to catch Michigan QB Bryce Underwood's pass.

After throwing to the back of the end zone on the first Hail Mary, Underwood threw towards the goal line on the second, and JJ Buchanan caught that pass for the Wolverines' win.

articles.title: La Champions estrena un parche para celebrar los debuts en la máxima competición europea
articles.standfirst: La UEFA reconocerá desde esta temporada a todos los futbolistas que disputen por primera vez un partido de la Liga de Campeones
articles.summary: La UEFA reconocerá desde esta temporada a todos los futbolistas que disputen por primera vez un partido de la Liga de Campeones
articles.body: La UEFA ha presentado el nuevo parche de debut de la UEFA Champions League, una iniciativa que entrará en vigor desde la temporada 2026/27 para distinguir a los futbolistas que disputen por primera vez un encuentro en la máxima competición continental de clubes. El distintivo estará integrado en el tradicional escudo 'Starball' que los jugadores lucen en la manga de sus camisetas. El proyecto ha sido desarrollado por la UEFA y UC3 en colaboración con Topps, con el objetivo de poner en valor uno de los momentos más importantes de la carrera de cualquier futbolista. El parche identificará de forma visible a aquellos jugadores que se estrenen en la Champions League, ya sea como titulares o entrando desde el banquillo. La novedad debutará en la primera jornada de la nueva temporada y permitirá que aficionados, clubes, operadores de televisión y socios comerciales reconozcan en tiempo real un acontecimiento especial dentro de la trayectoria deportiva de cada jugador. La UEFA considera que la iniciativa ayudará a reforzar el vínculo emocional entre los futbolistas y los seguidores. Equipos como el Como 1907, LASK, Viking y Sabah debutarán este curso en la Champions League, con lo que es más que posible que muchos de sus futbolistas portarán este parche. Por otro lado, entre los jugadores que podrían destacar en su debut en la máxima competición continental, uno de los que destaca es sin duda Yan Diomande y Carlos Espí. El nuevo jugador del Real Madrid, que jugó el pasado curso en el Leipzig, no sabe lo que es escuchar todavía el famoso himno previo de la competición. En el caso del Betis, sirva por ejemplo el de Álvaro Valles, que tras debutar el curso pasado en Europa League, este año lo hará en Champions. En el de Villarreal, Alex Freeman; y en cuanto al Barcelona y al Atlético de Madrid, salvo que tengan minutos canteranos, los nuevos fichajes todos tienen experiencia Champions Una vez concluido el partido del debut, el parche azul será retirado de la camiseta utilizada, autenticado y acompañado por un certificado oficial antes de ser entregado a Topps. Posteriormente, la compañía incorporará la pieza a una tarjeta coleccionable única, firmada por el propio jugador y destinada a convertirse en un objeto exclusivo para coleccionistas. La UEFA ha precisado que el distintivo solo podrá lucirse una vez en la carrera de cada futbolista. Tras su estreno en la Champions League, el jugador no volverá a llevar el parche, incluso aunque en el futuro cambie de club y continúe participando en competiciones europeas. De este modo, cada debut quedará inmortalizado como un momento irrepetible dentro de la historia del torneo.

articles.standfirst: El uruguayo fue con todo a la presión y confundió al portero del Inter en la acción del 2-0
articles.summary: El uruguayo fue con todo a la presión y confundió al portero del Inter en la acción del 2-0
articles.body: No es la primera vez que se ve una jugada así en la historia reciente del Real Madrid, pero sí llama la atención el cambio de protagonista. En esta ocasión fue Fede Valverde el que fue con hambre a la presión y provocó el cortocircuito del español Josep Martínez, el portero español del Inter, que llegó incluso a debutar con la absoluta en el partido del covid (2021). La acción de este martes en el Bernabéu se ha visto varias veces en los últimos años en el Madrid, casi siempre con Benzema como protagonista. El francés se la lió así a Ullrecih, portero suplente del Bayern, en todas unas semifinales de Champions, y también en el Bernabéu. También a Karius, en esa misma temporada, pero ya en la final, en una acción en la que se escondió tras el portero alemán para hacer el 1-0 en la final de Kiev ante el Liverpool. Pero, en puridad, la jugada recordó más a la del inevitable Karim en los octavos de final de la Champions de las remontadas (21-22), cuando la presión del francés hizo que Donnarumma perdiera el balón que fue aprovechado por Vinicius para asistir al 9. Fue el empate a uno en un partido bastante controlado por el PSG de Mbappé y Messi, que acabó aplstado por un triplete histórico de KB9.

articles.title: Karetsas, trasladado al hospital al sufrir problemas circulatorios durante el partido Dortmund - Villarreal
articles.standfirst: El club alemán comunicó que el futbolista se encuentra estable y será sometido a nuevas pruebas médicas tras abandonar el terreno de juego en camilla
articles.summary: El club alemán comunicó que el futbolista se encuentra estable y será sometido a nuevas pruebas médicas tras abandonar el terreno de juego en camilla
articles.body: La preocupación marcó los primeros compases del encuentro entre el Borussia Dortmund y el Villarreal después de que Konstantinos Karetsas tuviera que ser sustituido y evacuado en camilla tras sufrir un problema de salud sobre el terreno de juego. El club alemán informó posteriormente a través de sus canales oficiales de que el jugador griego presentó problemas circulatorios y que fue trasladado a un hospital para someterse a más pruebas médicas. Según el comunicado difundido por el Dortmund en su perfil oficial de la red social X, el jugador "se encuentra bien dentro de las circunstancias". El incidente se produjo mediada la primera parte, cuando Karetsas, de 18 años, pidió asistencia sin que existiera contacto previo con un rival. Tras entregar el balón a un compañero, el futbolista se detuvo y acabó tendido sobre el césped, lo que provocó una rápida intervención de los servicios médicos. El jugador permaneció varios minutos siendo atendido antes de abandonar el campo en camilla entre los aplausos de los aficionados presentes en el Signal Iduna Park. La escena generó enorme inquietud tanto en las gradas como en el banquillo local. Las cámaras captaron la preocupación del director general del Borussia Dortmund, Lars Ricken, mientras que el entrenador Niko Kovac siguió con atención la asistencia médica al joven atacante antes de que fuera trasladado fuera del terreno de juego. Karetsas llegó al Dortmund el pasado verano procedente del Genk. El futbolista griego había iniciado su etapa en dejando buenas sensaciones y estaba considerado una de las apuestas de futuro del club.
