articles.title: Aston Villa: Champions League victory in Brugge gives Villa lift-off with first win of season
articles.summary: Aston Villa finally found their shooting boots with three goals at Club Brugge - but their win was not straightforward.
articles.body:
It is a new chapter for Aston Villa and, against Club Brugge, they turned the page.

A first win of the season , albeit more nervy than anticipated, lit the spark for Unai Emery's side.

It may not have completely ignited the season yet but John McGinn, Emi Buendia and Nicolas Jackson gave them a winning Champions League return.

Villa won but could have drawn - or equally triumphed more handsomely - during a game which went from comfortable to edgy to relief.

It was only a second victory since that historic night in Istanbul when McGinn lifted the Europa League in May.

Since then it has been all change and, after another bleak Premier League opening, victory in Belgium was desperately needed.

With Fenerbahce and Viking to come at home in October, the path to Champions League progress is already opening up as Villa's new era slowly emerges.

The visitors were in a commanding and deserved position at half-time, McGinn's opener making him the club's all-time record European goalscorer with 12.

Buendia's strike and Jackson's first Villa goal - benefiting from Yann Sommer's rush of blood - had them cruising.

Brugge were poor and George Hemmings, Villa's first Champions League/European Cup teenage starter in 43 years, could have had at least one.

Yet the hosts made it uncomfortable for Emery's men with Nicolo Tresoldi's penalty after Aaron Wan-Bissaka's blatant handball setting up an anxious last half an hour, during which Tresoldi hit the post.

It can be viewed as a blessing in disguise that Villa had to battle their way through and ride out the hosts' pressure to earn their first win of the season. Adding the grit and determination to the quality of the opening half to prove they can get the job done.

Not that they needed the evidence themselves, Emery and his squad always have that faith and the internal desire to progress no matter the obstacle.

It was the same last season. A below-par 1-0 win over limited Bologna - thanks to another McGinn goal - got Villa going and they hardly looked back.

The victory kicked off the staggering run of 17 wins in 20 games which formed the backbone of returning to the Champions League and giving Villa momentum to win the Europa League.

Since then, of course, Villa's spine has been torn out and Emery has to integrate 10 new players into his methodical methods.

Three points in Brugge may not spark another relentless run but it gives Emery and Villa the foundations of this new era.

"It's a new Villa and it was a big test for the new players to dig in," McGinn told Uefa.

"It was Joao Gomes and George Hemmings' first Champions League game. It's not easy to go away at a place like this in difficult weather conditions. Club Brugge were pushing and pushing and pushing and we had to stand strong. We managed to do that.

"It was so important to show a real gritty performance and get a victory at a very, very tough place to play."

After just one shot on target in their opening three Premier League games the nine Villa had in Belgium would have been a comfort to Emery.

He said following Saturday's 0-0 draw at Hull it was vital to take the rebuild step-by-step and Tuesday's win was another positive move.

"The players have a responsibility too, the older players need to guide to keep our standard high, to show everybody that this is the only way to achieve our targets," Emery told the post-match news conference. "We are improving after Brighton and after Hull City .

"We must work hard - it is the only way. This is the process that we must try to set. We did one very important step forward, being resilient when we were struggling."

His players wasted no time in making that next leap by having 14 attempts in the first half, with Hemmings going closest to adding more goals.

Jackson, on his third start, got his first Villa goal following his record £65m move from Chelsea as he starts proving he is a fitting replacement for the departed Ollie Watkins.

The striker, who worked with Emery at Villarreal, will be one of the flag-bearers of Villa's new beginning as both the record signing and the player expected to score the goals to ensure they can compete at the elite level again.

"We don't care about the past, we just focus on the next one. Like every team, we have our ambitions. We just know it's a long journey, so we take it step by step try to win every game we play," said the Senegal international.

"I'm very happy to be here and happy to be with the team, manager and staff. Hopefully, there are many more to come."

Villa now host Nottingham Forest in the Premier League on Saturday before going to Coventry in the Carabao Cup and then travelling to Tottenham .

After returning from Belgium with three points following their stuttering start, they could go into the extended international break with a fresh perspective.

articles.title: Liverpool to replace Standard Chartered with Turkish Airlines in one of Premier League’s most lucrative £300m+ sponsorship deals
articles.summary: Football News: Liverpool Football Club announces a landmark £300 million sponsorship agreement with Turkish Airlines, set to take effect in June 2027, marking the end of its long-standing relationship with Standard Chartered.
articles.body: Liverpool have agreed a five-year sponsorship deal with Turkish Airlines worth more than £300million, with the airline set to become the club's new principal partner and front-of-shirt sponsor from next season.The agreement, which is reported to be worth in excess of £60million a year, will bring an end to Liverpool's 17-year relationship with Standard Chartered and see Turkish Airlines branding appear on the shirts of the men's, women's and academy teams from June 1, 2027.Liverpool believe the deal ranks among the most lucrative front-of-shirt agreements in Premier League history, with reports suggesting its value is comparable to major deals struck by Manchester United and Manchester City.The exact financial terms have not been disclosed by Liverpool, but media reports have valued the five-year package at more than £300million ($405.78million).Turkish Airlines replaces Standard Chartered after 17 yearsThe partnership marks a significant change to Liverpool's commercial identity, with Standard Chartered's 17-year run as the club's lead shirt sponsor coming to an end.However, Standard Chartered will not be leaving Liverpool altogether. The financial services company will remain involved as a Global Partner, while Turkish Airlines takes over the primary position in the club's commercial branding.The new agreement will also make Turkish Airlines only the third new front-of-shirt sponsor Liverpool have had in 35 years.Carlsberg occupied the front of Liverpool's shirts from 1992 until 2010, before Standard Chartered began its 17-year association with the club.Liverpool's most recent deal with Standard Chartered was understood to be worth around £50million per year, meaning the reported Turkish Airlines agreement represents a substantial increase.Liverpool chief commercial officer Ben Latty welcomed the new partnership and highlighted the connection between the club and Turkey.“This is a milestone announcement for us and we are delighted to welcome Turkish Airlines as our main club partner from June 2027,” Latty said.“The front of the Liverpool shirt holds a special place in the history of our club. Turkish Airlines is a globally recognised organisation with an extensive international network, and we look forward to beginning our partnership and building a strong relationship together, with already strong foundations built from those special memories back in 2005.”Latty's reference was to one of the most famous nights in Liverpool's history — the 2005 Champions League final in Istanbul, when Rafael Benitez's side famously came from 3-0 down against AC Milan before winning on penalties in what became known as the 'Miracle of Istanbul'.The new arrangement also expands Turkish Airlines' already significant presence in football. The airline is an official Champions League partner and the main sponsor of Turkey's national team.Turkish Airlines flies to more airports around the world than any of its competitors and is expected to make a major financial investment in its partnership with Liverpool.Liverpool's global reach behind record commercial dealThe agreement comes as Liverpool continue to emphasise the enormous global reach of their brand.The club believes that one Liverpool shirt is sold somewhere in the world every 20 seconds, while it also claims to have more standalone retail stores than any other football club.Liverpool recently expanded that retail network by opening a new store on Oxford Street in London.That international footprint is particularly relevant to a partnership with Turkish Airlines, whose own network spans a huge number of destinations around the world.The five-year agreement will therefore place Turkish Airlines prominently across Liverpool's men's, women's and academy teams, beginning with the 2027-28 season.For Liverpool, it represents a major commercial upgrade while ending one of the longest-running shirt sponsorship relationships in the Premier League.For Turkish Airlines, meanwhile, the deal provides a prominent association with one of the world's most recognisable football clubs and builds on its existing involvement with the Champions League and Turkish national team.The partnership will formally begin on June 1, 2027, when Turkish Airlines takes over the principal position from Standard Chartered.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El castigo de Oliver por el cambio de Vini que casi cuesta el empate
articles.standfirst: El brasileño demoró su salida y el Madrid estuvo más de un minuto con uno menos, sin que Carreras pudiera suplir al 7
articles.summary: El brasileño demoró su salida y el Madrid estuvo más de un minuto con uno menos, sin que Carreras pudiera suplir al 7
articles.body: El Bernabéu asistió en directo, y sufrió, uno de los cambios normativos de la nueva temporada. Michael Oliver, colegiado en el Madrid-Inter, interpretó que Vinicius demoró en exceso su salida del terreno de juego (el brasileño aplaudió a una grada que le dedicó pitos de forma ocasional) y castigó al Madrid. La pena fue jugar un minuto, que en realidad fue más, con un jugador menos, ya que Oliver no permitió la entrada en el terreno de juego de Álvaro Carreras, el cambio defensivo con el que Mourinho quiso cerrar el partido. Lo cierto es que, en medio de una enorme pitada del Bernabéu ante el paso de los segundos, el Inter estuvo a punto de aprovechar la superioridad numérica para empatar el partido. Tras una larga jugada, que se hizo eterna para los más de 70.000 madridistas presentes en el Bernabéu, el Inter encontró hueco por la banda izquierda. La jugada acabó en un tiro de Zielinski que sacó con muchos apuros Courtois, uno de los padres de una victoria muy sufrida. Otro gran partido del belga, que en la jugada posterior se impuso a Lautaro y abrochó la victoria del Madrid, que no acabó de convencer a su hinchada y que se vio dominado durante la mayor parte del partido por un buen Inter que finalmente se fue sin premio del Madrid.

articles.title: More Than Bragging Rights: Why Beating Chelsea Was Huge for Arsenal
articles.summary: Arsenal’s 2-1 victory over Chelsea was more than simply another London derby win. With Manchester City also making a perfect start to the campaign, Liam Hard...
articles.body:
Arsenal 's 2-1 victory over Chelsea was more than simply another London derby win. With Manchester City also making a perfect start to the campaign, Liam Harding believes beating the Blues was already one of the most important results of Arsenal's season.

Sunday's win was the most important of the season so far, despite Arsenal having only played three games during the 2026/27 campaign.

Even though Chelsea weren't fighting for the title after the midway point last season, with Arsenal in control, they've started pretty well and will of course be aiming to win their first Premier League title in ten seasons.

Two seasons ago, when Liverpool won the title, Chelsea were up there fighting with us for second and trying to pip the Merseysiders around the Christmas period. To say the least, they have challenged us in certain ways and also forced us to beat them earlier this year in the League Cup semi-final to reach the final, which we unfortunately lost.

Considering Manchester City, who will be pushing us for the title again, have won all three of their games following their marginal 1-0 victory over newly promoted Coventry City, it was absolutely paramount that we won.

The last thing we want is to be trailing the Citizens by two or three points at this stage of the season, when rapid momentum is needed. That may not predict what happens in the final stages of the campaign when the title may or may not be delivered, but hopefully it will be again.

When I saw we were 1-0 down after only two minues, I must admit I started to panic.

Even though it was early on, I thought if we conceded again it could be game over, but thanks to strikes from Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard , we eventually came out as 2-1 winners .

Despite my Great Grandad Ted Drake going on to win the league at Chelsea in 1955 as the first player and then manager to do so , following his triumphant stint in North London as a player, Arsenal runs stronger in my veins and I was seriously hoping that Arsenal could seal victory yesterday.

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Arsenal Must Keep Their Advantage Over Chelsea

It's important that we continue our winning streak against the Blues, who in the previous decade got the better of us more times than not, including that horrific 6-0 annihilation we faced at Stamford Bridge in 2014.

We certainly don't want to slip back into those complacent ways.

I don't think we will, but as they say, "nothing is impossible in football", and I don't think many Gooners thought we would lose 6-0 before that specific matchday either.

If Odegaard can steer clear of injury this season, then I don't see why we can't win a second league title, especially if Havertz continues his goalscoring form.

For now, beating Chelsea has maintained our momentum, kept us moving alongside our title rivals and, just as importantly, ensured London derby bragging rights remain with Arsenal.

articles.title: Whistles, boos & jeers: Real Madrid’s fans take aim at club’s stars during Inter Milan clash
articles.summary: The home crowd in attendance at La Liga giants Real Madrid’s meeting with Inter Milan on Tuesday made clear time and again their unhappiness with the level o...
articles.body:
The home crowd in attendance at La Liga giants Real Madrid 's meeting with Inter Milan on Tuesday made clear time and again their unhappiness with the level of performance conjured up by their side.

This comes after Los Blancos again looked some way short of their brilliant best…

José Mourinho's troops marked their return to action a short time ago, kicking the club's continental campaign into gear in a Champions League showdown with the aforementioned Inter Milan.

Real headed into proceedings with sights on a bounce-back performance, after a damaging first defeat of the term at Real Betis over the weekend.

When all was said and done, the evening's hosts did emerge on the right side of a 2-1 result. But safe to say, their performance was not exactly befitting of a side with hopes of going all the way in Europe this season.

Inter, for the most part, dominated possession and territory, with Real Madrid having played the game largely on the break.

This setup did not at all please those in attendance at the Bernabéu, who, throughout the 90 minutes, rained down on their own players with boos, whistles, jeers and more.

A winning start for Mourinho's men in the Champions League… But far from a perfect night for the competition's most successful team ever.

articles.title: UCL | Real Madrid 2-1 Inter: Costly errors ruin Champions League opener
articles.summary: Inter paid the price for embarrassing early errors in their 2-1 Champions League defeat to Real Madrid, but dominated possession for long periods and scored...
articles.body:
Inter paid the price for embarrassing early errors in their 2-1 Champions League defeat to Real Madrid , but dominated possession for long periods and scored through Carlos Augusto .

Treble winners Jose Mourinho and Cristian Chivu reunited on the touchline of the Bernabeu , with Denzel Dumfries facing his former teammates. The Nerazzurri missed Federico Dimarco and Djed Spence , but Curtis Jones got his first start for the club, with both Manuel Akanji and John Stones dropped.

The Merengues were fresh off a 1-0 defeat to Real Betis , with Bernardo Silva , Arda Guler and Eduardo Camavinga suspended, Eder Militao, Ferland Mendy , Raul Asencio and Rodrygo injured, plus Aurelien Tchouameni, Endrick and Thiago Pitarch not fully fit either. Mourinho therefore used Trent Alexander-Arnold in midfield for an unusual 4-2-3-1 formation.

MADRID, SPAIN – SEPTEMBER 08: Denzel Dumfries of Real Madrid interacts with a player of Internazionale before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Real Madrid C.F. and FC Internazionale Milano at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on September 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

It was a strong start from the visitors, Marcus Thuram forcing a save from eight yards on the Andy Diouf pull-back from eight yards, then Dean Huijsen twice made crucial blocks on Diouf and Hakan Calhanoglu .

MADRID, SPAIN – SEPTEMBER 08: Andy Diouf of Internazionale is challenged by Marc Cucurella of Real Madrid during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Real Madrid C.F. and FC Internazionale Milano at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on September 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Lautaro Martinez sting Thibaut Courtois ' gloves with a snapshot, but it was Real Madrid who took the lead entirely against the run of play.

The misplaced Jones pass caused problems for Yann Bisseck , allowing Brahim Diaz to thread through and send Kylian Mbappé clear on goal to squirm the finish under Josep Martinez.

Calhanoglu's screamer of a free kick tested Courtois, while Benjamin Pavard timed the tackle perfectly to stop Vinicius Junior scoring when pouncing on another error.

MADRID, SPAIN – SEPTEMBER 08: Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid is challenged by Yann Aurel Bisseck and Benjamin Pavard of Internazionale during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Real Madrid C.F. and FC Internazionale Milano at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on September 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Inter shot themselves in the foot even more spectacularly for the second goal, as Josep Martinez tried a cheeky turn to dribble away from Federico Valverde in his six-yard box, but made a complete hash of it, allowing the prod into an empty net.

Having dominated possession and going 2-0 down, their confidence was shaken with only a desperate Bisseck tackle preventing the third goal from Mbappé.

Jones turned and clipped the top of the crossbar from 14 yards, but Josep Martinez denied a third goal with an extraordinary double save. He stuck out a foot to deny Mbappé, then somehow managed to get his glove to the Jude Bellingham tap-in, as Brahim Diaz turned the third attempt onto the upright.

Inter had 67 per cent possession in that first half and completed 333 passes to 127, yet were trailing 2-0 after gifting goals with errors.

John Stones replaced Pavard for the second half, but Josep Martinez rushed off his line to make the save when Mbappé sprinted away on the counter from an Inter corner.

Courtois was also alert to deny Jones on another Diouf assist, while Marcus Thuram volleyed a Calhanoglu low cross over from nine yards, and Lautaro Martinez couldn't control a Calhanoglu through ball when springing the offside trap.

Bellingham really should've made it 3-0 on 58 minutes when Brahim Diaz floated in a ball from the by-line, but he insisted on taking a touch first rather than nodding over from close range, allowing Josep Martinez to scramble back and make the huge save.

Courtois was also decisive, getting down to parry the ferocious Alessandro Bastoni daisy-cutter, and Martinez reacted well to deny Mbappé from 12 yards on the Brahim Diaz roll across.

Brahim Diaz's angled drive flashed wide after a well-worked team move, with Bisseck bravely getting his face in the way of a Valverde scorcher.

Inter finally got their goal when Lautaro Martinez pulled back from the right by-line for Carlos Augusto to sweep in from six yards.

Yan Diomande came off the bench and the €125m signing tested Josep Martinez at the near post, but Henrikh Mkhitaryan also stung Courtois' gloves with a deflected effort.

articles.title: Dembele, Mbappe, Kane and Yamal top Ballon d’Or shortlist
articles.summary: Ballon d’Or Ousmane Dembele among favourites, with Kylian Mbappe, Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane, as 2026 shortlist named.
articles.body:
Last year’s winner Ousmane Dembele, as well as Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe, are among the top contenders for the men’s Ballon d’Or.

The 30 men’s and 30 women’s nominees were revealed by France Football magazine on Tuesday, with the winners to be announced at a ceremony in London on October 26.

In the women’s field, two-time winner Alexia Putellas, Ewa Pajor and Melchie Dumornay are among the favourites. Aitana Bonmatí, the winner of the past three awards, did not make the cut after missing most of the season through injury. She returned at the end of Barcelona’s quadruple-winning season that included another Champions League title.

Dembele and Mbappe both played for France at the World Cup, where their team lost to the eventual champion, Spain, in the semifinals. Although it is difficult to win the accolade without a major trophy, Mbappe made history when he overtook Lionel Messi for the most all-time World Cup goals (22) in fewer games.

After claiming a second straight Champions League title with Paris Saint-Germain, Dembele has a chance to retain the Ballon d’Or.

Kane had one of his best seasons, scoring 73 goals for club and country and winning the Bundesliga title with Bayern Munich. Kane also led England to a third-place finish at the World Cup.

Spain captain Rodri, who claimed the award in 2024 and played an instrumental role in midfield to help Spain secure its second World Cup title, was also included.

The 39-year-old Messi, who has a record eight Ballon d’Or awards, was on the shortlist after guiding Argentina to a runner-up finish at the World Cup and winning Major League Soccer with Inter Miami. The other three Ballon d’Or winners still active, Karim Benzema, Cristiano Ronaldo, and Luka Modric, were not on the list.

Dembele was one of nine PSG players – 10 including newly acquired Ferran Torres – nominated for the men’s award, alongside Achraf Hakimi, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, Willian Pacho, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Joao Neves, Fabian Ruiz and Vitinha. Torres scored Spain’s winner in the World Cup final.

In an interview with France Football, Dembele said he expects the award to remain at PSG. Asked to name his top three in no particular order, he cited PSG teammate Kvaratskhelia, Kane and Mbappe. He also mentioned Michael Olise, Lamine Yamal, Ruiz and Pacho, but did not include himself.

“I don’t think the trophy is undecided. I think it will remain in the hands of a Paris Saint-Germain player,” he said.

The other men’s nominees include Real Madrid stars Vinicius Junior and Jude Bellingham, as well as Manchester City striker Erling Haaland.

Italy, which did not qualify for the World Cup, and the Netherlands and Germany had no representatives. Only one player from Serie A, Lautaro Martínez of Inter Milan, was selected.

There was no goalkeeper nominated, ensuring Lev Yashin remains the only keeper to win the coveted trophy (1963) for another year.

The Ballon d’Or ceremony is moving from its traditional Paris home to London this year to mark the 70th anniversary of the first award won by England great Stanley Matthews.

The Ballon d’Or was created by France Football and has been awarded since 1956 for men, and since 2018 for women. It is voted for by journalists from the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings for the men’s award and the top 50 FIFA-ranked countries for the women’s award.

Each journalist, one per country, selects players in ranked order with points attributed to each position. The winner is the player who receives the most points.

Organisers say the trophy is awarded based on three criteria, in order of importance: 1, individual performances, decisive and impressive character; 2, collective performances and titles won; 3, class and fair play. The performance period is August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 — the day of this year’s World Cup final.

articles.title: El Bernabéu se marcha preocupado
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Real Madrid - Inter de Milan
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Real Madrid - Inter de Milan
articles.body: El Bernabéu se marchó preocupado. Porque el resultado dijo una cosa y el partido contó otra muy distinta. El equipo italiano fue superior en casi todo: tuvo más balón, dio más pases, generó más ocasiones y manejó durante muchos minutos el ritmo del encuentro. Ganó casi todas las estadísticas. Todas menos la única que realmente importa, la de los goles. Y ahí el Madrid volvió a agarrarse a esa capacidad casi inexplicable para sobrevivir cuando peor pinta tiene la noche. Especialidad de la casa en Champions. Brahim, Courtois y Mbappé fueron la excepción al tono gris del Madrid y también la mejor noticia. Eléctrico y atrevido el malagueño. Salvador Tibu. Y letal Kylian. Pero ya. El resto dejó demasiadas preguntas para una noche de Champions que terminó con victoria, pero sin celebración completa. Y entre esas preguntas vuelve a aparecer Vinícius. Hay ‘runrún’ con el brasileño y el Bernabéu ya no disimula cuando algo no le gusta. Sigue lejos de su mejor versión y cada pérdida empieza a generar murmullos en una grada que espera mucho más de él. El portero del Inter firmó en el Bernabéu el peor error de su carrera tras perder el balón ante Fede Valverde dentro del área pequeña. Recibió el balón, intentó un regate... y al uruguayo solo le hizo falta entrar en contacto con la pelota para convertir esa presión en gol. Error garrafal del portero que dará la vuelta al mundo, pese a que luego protagonizaría dos de las paradas de la noche. Primero con el pie a Mbappé, luego desde el segundo a Bellingham. Un dos en uno de muchísimo mérito en la primera parte que repetiría, otra vez con Jude, en la segunda. Pese a todo, seguro que no olvida la pifia en el 2-0. La noche en el Bernabéu valió la pena por la jugada de Brahim en el minuto 58. El malagueño recibió el balón en el vértice del área y llegó a línea de fondo tras dos regates espectaculares, uno de ellos arrastrando el balón de tacón. Puro Brahim, que fue más genial aún asistiendo a Bellingham. Un pase que fue pura magia, picando el balón por encima del portero. Fallaría la ocasión Bellingham, con paradón de Josep Martínez, y Brahim se quedaría sin la asistencia de la noche. Para las estadísticas, el primer gol de Kylian sí que lleva su sello tras robar la pelota y dejar solo al francés para hacer el 1-0. El mejor del Madrid ante el Inter. El Inter fue una máquina de generar fútbol, sobre todo en la primera parte, pero le condenaron los errores individuales. Dos pérdidas de balón que dieron lugar a los dos goles del Real Madrid, sometido en todos los aspectos del juego. La posesión fue para el Inter, que tuvo el balón el 63% del tiempo (70 al descanso). 577 pases del equipo italiano, por 305 del Madrid. Más córners también para el Inter: diez a tres. También ganó más duelos y robó más balones el equipo interista. Pero lo que cuentan son los goles y el Madrid marcó dos en la primera parte y el Inter solo uno en la segunda. Eso sí, el Bernabéu se dio cuenta de lo que había... Cómo no se va a enfadar Mbappé cuando le quieren culpar de los males del Madrid... o de los males del pasado del PSG. Kylian hace temporada tras temporada lo que tiene que hacer, que es marcar goles. El delantero empezó la noche levantando el trofeo de máximo goleador de la última Champions y a los 14 minutos ya estaba marcando el primero en esta edición. Un gol, por cierto, con el que igualaba los 71 tantos en Champions de Raúl González. Si todos los jugadores del Madrid hicieran su trabajo como Mbappé... Courtois hizo seis paradas de gol ante el Inter, abortando cualquier opción de remontada del equipo italiano. El belga firmó intervenciones de todos los colores y confirmó una noche más que es el mejor portero del mundo. Una buena noticia a medias, claro, porque el Inter desnudó en demasiadas ocasiones el entramado defensivo del equipo blanco. Courtois, que nada pudo hacer en el gol del Inter, evitó una noche de pesadilla. Hay ‘runrún’ con Vinicius en el Bernabéu. El brasileño sigue sin encontrar su mejor versión y la paciencia de la afición madridista empieza a agotarse. No hubo una pitada masiva, pero sí se escucharon voces discordantes cada vez que perdió el balón, y fueron unas cuantas. También en el campo se escuchó música de viento. En la primera parte logró arrancar los aplausos de la grada por pelear una pelota junto a la banda, pero aquella acción aislada no sirvió para maquillar otro partido gris. Vinicius busca reencontrarse mientras el Bernabéu, de momento, espera… aunque ya empieza a hacerlo con cierto ruido de fondo. La Champions arrancó en el Santiago Bernabéu sin la clásica lona de las estrellas en el centro del campo. Raro, raro. Cuesta creer que se le olvidara a la UEFA o que se quedaran sin voluntarios para levantarla. Un misterio que sorprendió a los presentes en el Bernabéu pero que no restó mística al inicio del encuentro.

articles.title: Could SEC vote to expel LSU cancel Tennessee game, Lane Kiffin's return? Latest updates
articles.summary: The SEC is set to vote on LSU's future in the conference Sept. 10.
articles.body:
Tennessee football's schedule could be impacted by the SEC's ongoing legal battle with LSU .

The SEC claims it has the authority to expel LSU from the conference in an amended complaint on Sept. 8 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama, USA TODAY reported . There will also be a meeting Sept. 10 to vote on the future of LSU's membership in the league, according to the brief.

The No. 18 Vols (1-0) are scheduled to host the No. 8 Tigers (1-0) at Neyland Stadium on Nov. 21. It will be new LSU coach Lane Kiffin's first time back at Neyland Stadium since 2021, which famously ended with Tennessee fans hitting the former UT coach with a golf ball while throwing debris on the field .

The vote follows the SEC filing a lawsuit against LSU and Kiffin on Sept. 3 over player eligibility. Kiffin added former Ole Miss players Zxavian Harris and Dae'Quan Wright, who were on NFL rosters, to his LSU roster after a court order gave them eligibility. Neither Harris or Wright played in the Tigers' blowout win over Clemson in the season opener, which the Tigers won 51-10.

The SEC argues in the briefing that LSU lacks institutional control. The brief supports that argument by citing Kiffin's comments at halftime of the Clemson matchup, when Kiffin "commented that the score differential would have been even greater if LSU had played professional players."

Yahoo's Ross Dellenger reported Sept. 8 reported that 11 of the 16 SEC presidents have to support expulsion for it to pass.

articles.title: Borja Iglesias: “He rentabilizado 3 minutos para un título más en mi palmarés”
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Celta bromea en La Revuelta sobre su participación en el Mundial
articles.summary: El delantero del Celta bromea en La Revuelta sobre su participación en el Mundial
articles.body: Borja Iglesias intervino este martes, por videollamada, en La Revuelta y se tomó con humor su escasa participación en el Mundial: “He rentabilizado 3 minutos para un título más en mi palmarés. Toqué un balón y se me escapó el control. A Unai Simón le quiero mucho pero el saque venía en la línea”. También se refirió al buen ambiente en el grupo de Luis de la Fuente: “Ha sido muy bonito porque la gente se ha identificado con un grupo bastante variopinto y eso creo que ha sido muy bonito para España. Hacia fuera de España también he sentido que la gente ha visto una victoria de grupo, de equipo, que no es tan sencillo". Borja Iglesias no pudo asistir en vivo al programa, al estar aún buscando su mejor estado de forma tras la lesión sufrida las últimas semanas: “Vengo de una lesión y me han hecho volver para seguir tratándome. Llevo unas semanitas de bastante carga de trabajo y ayer acabé bastante cansado y eso que jugué 20 minutos. Acabé cansadísimo". El delantero céltico, también bromeando, se comprometió a asistir al programa antes del próximo mes de marzo, fecha en la cual se especula que podrían tener lugar las próximas elecciones generales.

articles.title: Así está la clasificación de la Champions League en la primera jornada: Real Madrid y Betis se colocan en lo más alto
articles.standfirst: Así queda tras el primer día de enfrentamientos
articles.summary: Así queda tras el primer día de enfrentamientos
articles.body: La nueva edición de la Liga de Campeones echa a andar con el arranque de la esperada fase de liga. Los principales clubes continentales buscan sumar sus primeros tres puntos para tomar posiciones tempranas. Real Madrid, Manchester City, Aston Villa, AEK de Atenas, Betis y Dortmund lograron sumar la primera victoria. Fueron resultados ajustados, salvo el del equipo de Maresca que ganó con un doblete de Haaland. Muy importantes fueron los tres puntos cosechados por los verdiblancos en Lille, teniendo que remontar en dos ocasiones, regresando 21 años después por la puerta grande. La máxima competición europea estrena curso con la disputa de una vibrante primera jornada repartida a lo largo de tres días seguidos. Los conjuntos favoritos saltan al terreno de juego sabiendo que sumar triunfos desde el inicio resulta vital para evitar cruces complicados y no tener que hacer cuentas en las últimas jornadas. Esta emocionante fecha inicial pondrá a prueba el nivel físico de las plantillas de élite, que buscan situarse rápidamente en la zona alta que otorga el billete directo. En este innovador sistema de competición, los ocho primeros clasificados al finalizar la liguilla obtienen el billete directo a los octavos de final. Por su parte, los clubes situados entre la novena y la vigesimocuarta posición disputarán una eliminatoria de repesca a doble partido para completar la fase eliminatoria. Finalmente, los equipos que terminen entre el puesto veinticinco y el treinta y seis quedarán eliminados de forma definitiva de la competición.

articles.title: El Villarreal se estrella otra vez en el muro de Dortmund
articles.standfirst: El submarino dio una buena imagen ante un rival muy efectivo que aprovechó un penalti discutible para desnivelar el encuentro
articles.summary: El submarino dio una buena imagen ante un rival muy efectivo que aprovechó un penalti discutible para desnivelar el encuentro
articles.body: El Villarreal peleó hasta el final, pero terminó cayendo otra vez en Dortmund. El submarino jugó con personalidad en un escenario imponente y se sobrepuso a los goles de un equipo alemán siempre efectivo. Además, se encontró con un dudoso penalti en contra que, al final, desniveló la balanza, en un partido marcado por los problemas de salud de Karetsas, que tuvo que ser trasladado al hospital. No parecía el Villarreal un equipo con dudas tras su mal arranque en Liga ni mucho menos impresionado por el escenario. El equipo de Iñigo Pérez exhibió carácter como para discutirle el balón al Dortmund y, sobre todo, para fabricarse buenas ocasiones, tras un primer aviso de Pau Navarro de cabeza a la salida de un córner. Buchanan puso después un buen centro que Mikautadze no supo cómo rematar en el segundo palo. Después llegó la lesión de Karetsas, que tuvo que salir en camilla tras dejarse caer solo sobre el césped. Le sustituyó Nwaneri, que movió bien al equipo alemán en los metros finales. Pero el submarino mantuvo el plan de partido, multiplicando efectivos en la presión y saliendo a la carrera cuando recuperaban el balón. A punto estuvo Buchanan de adelantar a su equipo antes del descanso, con un gran disparo que Kobel detuvo en dos tiempos. El Dortmund aceleró tras el paso por los vestuarios y, a las primeras de cambio, Nwaneri estrelló un disparo lejano en la base del poste cuando Gulacsi ya batido estaba batido. El gol del equipo alemán llegó más por acumulación que por dominio. Y también por el infortunio de Renato Veiga que remató a su portería un buen centro de Beier desviado por el portero. No se descompuso el Villarreal. Al contrario. Antes de empatar Mouriño a la salida de un córner, Oluwaseyi y Comesaña estuvieron muy cerca de marcar. Pero fue el lateral uruguayo el que puso la igualada tras un buen servicio de Mikautadze. El Villarreal amagó con buscar la victoria, pero fueron los cambios de Kovac los que desnivelaron el encuentro. En el 80’ Jobe Bellingham conectó con Fabio Silva que asistió para la llegada de Guirassy al segundo palo. Y después, el delantero guineano marcó el 3-1 de penalti, de los que forcejean defensor y atacante. El autogol de Guirassy, en un gran disparo de Pépé, dio vida en el tiempo añadido en el Villarreal que tuvo el empate en las botas de Renato Veiga.

articles.title: Southampton 3-1 Swansea: Cyle Larin scores again as Saints knock Vitor Matos' side off top of Championship
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Southampton and Swansea City at St Mary's on Tuesday night; goals from Finn Azaz, Cyle Larin and Leo Scienza help Saints to a comprehensive win
articles.body:
Larin, who is the joint-top scorer in the Championship, netted either side of Finn Azaz and Leo Scienza strikes to make it 13 games unbeaten at St Mary's in a row.

It followed Saints hammering previous leaders Millwall 5-1 10 days ago, although Swansea - who netted through Zan Vipotnik's penalty - stayed level on points at the summit.

Swansea made five changes from the side which drew with Wrexham at the weekend and failed to have a shot on target in the first half - with the majority of their efforts blocked long before reaching Daniel Peretz.

On the other hand, the hosts were rampant as they eased through the Swans' lines.

Scienza and Ryan Manning were the first to find open spaces behind their opposition in the fourth minute, but after their neat interchange, Azaz skied high into the stand.

But five minutes later the Republic of Ireland international found the bottom corner with a low left-footed shot, after Flynn Downes had powered through.

It was Azaz's first goal in seven attempts against Swansea, his second of the season, and just the second goal the Swans had conceded in 2026-27.

Larin was the second player to go from putting supporters in the Chapel Stand at risk before scoring.

The Canadian snatched at a half-volley after a corner in the 25th minute, before sliding home eight minutes later.

This time James Bree had made the run in behind the porous defence before squaring to Larin for his fifth league strike of the campaign, after two blanks.

Midfielder Downes had an opportunity to completely put the game to bed two minutes before the interval but he hooked over the crossbar after a Larin knockdown.

Swansea boss Vitor Matos sent winger Ronald on at half-time and he brought immediate energy by bundling a shot over.

It was contagious for the away side, and within 10 minutes of the restart they had pulled a goal back.

Bree pulled back Vipotnik at the back post before the Slovenian picked himself up to fire into the bottom left corner from the spot - his seventh straight penalty success.

Despite a far more even balance of play, Southampton still had the better chances, as Keven Schlotterbeck's poke forced a good save and Larin's improvised header bounced narrowly wide.

And Scienza - who had seen a lashed shot battered away - secured the three points 12 minutes from the end by calmly slotting into the corner after being released by Kuryu Matsuki.

articles.title: Cardiff 1-1 Stoke: Joel Colwill earns Bluebirds a point but winless start on Championship return continues
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Cardiff City and Stoke City at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday night; Joel Colwill's header cancels out Ben Johnson's opener to earn Bluebirds a point
articles.body:
Stoke had hope of an away-day success after a run of nine straight Sky Bet Championship defeats when Ben Johnson scored midway through the first half.

But the Potters came under fierce pressure in the second half and Joel Colwill's headed home for Cardiff hosts who hit a post three times.

The draw - Cardiff's fourth in six games - was enough to take the Bluebirds out of the relegation zone, while Stoke slip to 15th.

Krystian Bielik was named in the Cardiff starting line-up after being involved in a physical altercation with a fan at Portsmouth on Saturday.

The incident is currently the subject of an investigation by Hampshire Police.

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy had urged supporters and players to stay calm after a tricky start and two successive defeats that had dropped them into the relegation zone.

Stoke had been boosted by back-to-back home wins but their form on the road was dire, with no wins in 11 games.

Ollie Tanner had two chances in the space of 60 seconds for the Bluebirds.

A slick interchange of passes between Tanner, Jack Moylan and Yousef Salech allowed the winger space and his shot from 20 yards struck the base of a post.

Stoke escaped again immediately as goalkeeper Viktor Johansson, under pressure from Salech, sent his clearing kick straight to Tanner, who failed to find an empty net from a tight angle.

Robert Bozenik skewed Stoke's first opening wide, but the Potters were ahead after Tanner failed to convert at the far post.

Bozenik played the ball over the top of the Cardiff defence and Johnson profited from some weak defending to open his account on a season-long loan from Ipswich.

George Hirst forced Nathan Trott to shovel his effort from 20 yards, and the Cardiff goalkeeper had to react again to hold Justin Devenny's deflected shot.

Good chances came thick and fast at the start of the second half after Moylan fired straight at Johansson.

Hirst was clean through but he lacked conviction approaching Trott and the goalkeeper saved with his legs.

Tanner then burst away after dispossessing Luke Graham, but Ben Wilmot came to Stoke's rescue with a brilliant block that earned him high-fives all round.

Colwill met Chris Willock's cross after 63 minutes to broke Stoke's resistance, looping a header on to a post and past Johansson.

The same combination almost paid dividends for Cardiff moments later when another Colwill header thumped off a post.

Salech had two clear-cut chances late on and Moylan struck the goal frame in stoppage time as Cardiff were frustrated.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Watford 2-1 Preston: Mamadou Doumbia winner condemns Paul Heckingbottom's North End suffer fifth defeat in six
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Watford and Preston North End at Vicarage Road on Tuesday night; Edo Kayembe and Mamadou Doumbia seal Hornets comeback to condemn Paul Heckingbottom's side to a fifth defeat in six
articles.body:
Callum Lang had shot the visitors ahead in the sixth minute as the visitors threatened to overrun the Hornets, who hit back with two second-half goals in seven minutes from Edo Kayembe and Mamadou Doumbia.

Injuries meant that Watford boss Alessio Dionisi was limited to eight substitutes - including two goalkeepers.

But the Hornets made a lively start, with winger Rocco Vata breaking into the box from the left only to see his shot blocked by Preston keeper Daniel Iversen.

The visitors replied by scoring from their first attack.

Johnny Kenny, in his first start for Preston, won a corner on the left, Alfie Devine's kick found Jordan Thompson just outside the D via a smart stepover by Leo Leroy and the midfielder fired in a shot that home keeper Federico Ravaglia could only push on to his left-hand post.

Lang pounced on the rebound to score from close range despite Ravaglia's efforts to scoop the ball to safety - Lang's third goal in two games.

Preston should have gone 2-0 up in the 18th minute. Kenny sprinted down the left with the home defence nowhere and his perfect cross found the feet of Lang, who fired straight at Ravaglia.

Nevertheless, the visitors continued to look by far the better, more composed side as they dominated the first half.

Dionisi rolled the dice at the break, sending on Othmane Maamma, Iker Bravo and Leicester loanee Stephy Mavididi in place of Rocco Vata, Martin Payero and Amin Nabizada.

However, as the second half wore on, it seemed that Preston would stretch their unbeaten run at Vicarage Road to five games.

The Hornets threatened very little, and their first raid after the break came in the 55th minute when skipper and centre-back Mattie Pollock ventured upfield only to fire over the bar.

There should have been more woe for the Vicarage Road faithful just before the hour when Preston wasted another great chance.

Lilywhites defender Harry Clarke was allowed to take a stroll through the home box but scuffed his shot, allowing Ravaglia to push the ball against the post before scrambling it to safety.

Preston should have been at least 3-0 up, and they paid dearly for those misses when Kayembe equalised in the 69th minute.

Maamma had been switching wings and his time he danced in from the left before his low cross set up a gleeful Kayembe for the leveller.

Preston lost the plot as Watford seized the lead seven minutes later. The threat this time came down the right as Bravo crossed for striker Doumbia to head home from a narrow angle.

articles.title: Blackburn 1-2 Sheffield United: Sydie Peck scores one and sets up another as Blades come from behind to win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United at Ewood Park on Tuesday night; Sydie Peck scores one and sets up the other as Chris Wilder's Blades sealed their second win in three games
articles.body:
All goals came in a first half that Rovers dominated and deservedly took the lead in through Kristi Montgomery's first goal for the club on 20 minutes.

The Blades were blunted without a shot in anger for the first 34 minutes but they turned the game on its head with goals from their only two shots of the half as Tom Cannon stroked home a second on this ground in two weeks in the 35th minute.

And Sydie Peck rifled home his first of the season a minute before the break to complete the turnaround.

Hamza Choudhury's sensational goalline block preserved the lead in the second half, along with two smart Michael Cooper saves. But it was the spell of clinical finishing that made the difference as Chris Wilder's men moved to within two points of the league summit.

Blackburn's encouraging start was rewarded in the 20th minute when Montgomery dispossessed Peck and whipped the ball emphatically into the top right corner from 20 yards out.

They went close to doubling the advantage six minutes later when Jayden Fevrier, on his first Rovers start, broke forward for the hosts and released Dapo Afolayan on the left whose strike whistled just beyond the far post.

Cantwell had the ball in the net in the 35th minute when Mike Cooper could only parry Afolayan's fierce strike but the offside flag saved his blushes.

It proved vital as the Blades were level within a minute with their first effort of any note when Peck atoned for his part in the Blackburn goal by threading an inch perfect ball for Cannon on the left who calmy slotted under Aynsley Pears into the bottom right corner.

Peck had his pocket picked again minutes later after Romelle Donovan played him into trouble but Fevrier's low drive was deflected just wide of the right-hand post.

But Rovers fell behind in the 44th minute when Peck collected Joe Rothwell's pass and brilliantly flicked over Tom Atcheson before hammering into the bottom left corner.

Blackburn's best chance came in the 57th minute when the visitors failed to clear and the ball fell to Afolayan six yards out with just Choudhury to beat but the defender remarkably blocked.

Ryan Alebiosu directed a shot just wide midway through the half when set clear before Yuri Rubeiro kept Rovers in the game in the 72nd minute, clearing off the line after Sam McCallum's shot squired under Pears.

Cooper made a smart stop low to his right to deny Fevrier with eight minutes to go and Blades held on to condemn Rovers to consecutive defeats.

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Sunderland 1-0 Hull City: Chemsdine Talbi's delightful dink enough to send dominant Black Cats through in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Sunderland and Hull at the Stadium of Light; Chemsdine Talbi's superb dink enough to see Black Cats into fourth round
articles.body:
A lacklustre meeting at the Stadium of Light between the two Premier League sides eventually saw Talbi's chipped finish put the Black Cats ahead 71 minutes in.

His effort was enough to book Sunderland's spot in the fourth round of the competition, which takes place at the end of October.

Regis Le Bris made 11 changes from the squad who drew with Brentford at the weekend, with Dayann Methalie and Jules Ahoka handed their debuts alongside a full debut for Malick Fofana, who came off the bench against the Bees.

Sergej Jakirovic also shuffled his pack with eight switches from their goalless stalemate against Aston Villa, including full debuts for Mohamed-Ali Cho, Sorba Thomas and Robinio Vaz.

Dillon Phillips was called into action early to claw Jocelin Ta Bi's cross over the bar and the goalkeeper made a solid dive to push away Ahoka's header as Sunderland looked to strike early.

Hull had successive corners cleared as the half fizzled into a quiet affair, with both teams seeing the ball but struggling to test either goalkeeper.

Sunderland suddenly threatened when the ball reached Chris Rigg and the teenager played a pass into Jocelin, but the winger scuffed his shot wide.

Talbi raced into the box and forced Phillips into a low stop before Ahoka blazed an effort over from distance.

Just before the break, Vaz had a tame shot from a tight angle claimed by Melker Ellborg.

Sunderland went close after the restart when Wilson Isidor's looping header landed on the roof of the net and Rigg curled a free-kick wide.

Hull made a triple substitution in the 59th minute and soon tested Ellborg when Thomas' free-kick was parried away by the Sunderland goalkeeper.

However, the Black Cats eventually broke the deadlock with 19 minutes to play when they broke from a Hull corner.

Substitute Thomas Meunier flicked the ball to Talbi, who raced through the visiting defence before coolly chipping the ball over Phillips into the bottom corner.

Isidor skewed an effort wide as Sunderland looked to wrap up the win and substitute Timur Tutierov blasted over.

In a late surge, Hull searched for the equaliser when former Black Cat loanee Joe Gelhardt scuffed an effort over the bar from close range and Cho fired wide from a corner, but Sunderland saw the game out.

articles.title: Bournemouth 4-0 Lincoln: Ryan Christie hat-trick helps Cherries demolish Imps in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup third round tie between Bournemouth and Lincoln at the Vitality Stadium; Ryan Christie hits hat-trick before Rayan’s late fourth in dominant home win
articles.body:
The Scotland international starred for the hosts with goals in the seventh, 69th and 88th minutes for his second career hat-trick, with Rayan stepping off the bench to wrap up the Carabao Cup third-round victory in stoppage time.

Rose made eight changes, including handing a debut to on-loan Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio and a first start for Uruguayan striker Alvaro Rodriguez.

Only Ryley Towler kept his place from Lincoln's 1-1 draw at home to Southampton as the two sides met for the first time since 2010 when they were both in League Two.

Lincoln started brightly, but it was Bournemouth who opened the scoring after just seven minutes when Christie finished neatly at the near post from Ben Gannon-Doak's cross.

The lively Gannon-Doak then saw his effort blocked by Towler after cutting in from the left wing and firing a right-footed shot.

Di Gregorio was called into action for the first time after 22 minutes, keeping out Dan Oyegoke's flick before Towler blazed over from the rebound.

Lincoln goalkeeper Joe Gauci made a smart save to deny Bafode Diakite after the defender had headed a long throw goalwards.

James Hill then fired over from distance as Bournemouth went hunting for a second goal. Six minutes before half-time Cherries left-back Julio Soler curled wide from 25 yards after David Brooks' corner had been only half cleared.

Hill also saw a shot from the edge of the penalty area deflected behind for a corner, before Christie's curling 20-yard effort was palmed away by Gauci with the final kick of the first half.

Rose will be frustrated to have picked up just two points from his first three Premier League games after conceding late goals against Manchester City, Everton and Newcastle.

His side almost doubled their lead five minutes into the second half when Gannon-Doak's curling effort glanced off the head of Rodriguez and flew just over the crossbar.

Scotland international Gannon-Doak then ballooned another long-range effort over in the 55th minute.

Hill came close to picking out the top corner with a 25-yard piledriver which smacked against the angle of post and crossbar.

Rodriguez had another good chance to open his Bournemouth account moments later, but slipped as he lined up a shot from the edge of the box and sent it high into the stands.

The £21m signing later headed inches wide from Hill's cross as he endured a frustrating full debut.

Christie showed Rodriguez the route to goal 21 minutes from time by heading in Brooks' corner at the far post.

The Scotland midfielder completed his treble in the 88th minute with a deflected shot from 14 yards out after being teed up by Diakite.

Rayan made it 4-0 in stoppage time with a tidy finish from the corner of the six-yard box.

articles.title: FC Porto 0-2 Manchester City: Erling Haaland earns Enzo Maresca a first Champions League win as City head coach but English side fail to impress
articles.summary: Report as Manchester City beat FC Porto 2-0 away from home in Enzo Maresca's first Champions League game in charge of the club; Erling Haaland put missed chances in the first half behind him to score the winner after 47 minutes, then netted a second in stoppage time
articles.body:
City's main man up front was surprisingly wasteful in the first half, seeing two glorious chances in the area saved by Diogo Costa as well as heading another good chance over the bar.

Porto's goalkeeper was in inspired form in the opening 45 minutes, also saving well from Rayan Cherki from the rebound of one of Haaland's chances.

But Haaland took just two minutes of the second period to make amends, barging Jakub Kiwior aside to nod an Enzo Fernandez cross in off the post.

But City then took their foot off the gas as the Portuguese champions started to grow in confidence. Porto failed to produce a shot on target but Alan Varela curled just wide of the far post from the edge of the box in a warning shot.

Then Gianluigi Donnarumma was nearly caught in possession by Porto forward William Gomes, with the City goalkeeper lucky to see the ball run away to safety. City did find a way to seal the result, however, as Haaland tucked home Rayan Ait-Nouri's cutback in stoppage time.

Despite another game this season where City have won but struggled to impress at the same time, Maresca failed to win away of his three away Champions League ties as Chelsea boss last term. He will see a winning start to this campaign as a positive.

But improvement is needed ahead of Sunday's Manchester derby at Old Trafford, live on Sky Sports .

16: SAVE! Antoine Semenyo starts the game brightly and curls an early effort into Diogo Costa's gloves.

21: BIG CHANCE FOR HAALAND! Semenyo feeds Phil Foden who clips a cross into the box for Haaland - who is denied by a smart glove from Costa.

27: BIG MISS! Haaland heads over another good chance via a cross from the left, this time from Semenyo.

29: BIG SAVE! Foden goes on a mazy run in and around the penalty area and forces another save from Costa.

31: DOUBLE SAVE! A man possessed! Costa denies Haaland's low drive from inside the box, then gets up to stop Rayan Cherki at the rebound.

42: OUCH! Marc Guehi catches Gabri Veiga with his arm which causes a lot of blood. With Porto calling for a red card for a violent elbow, the Man City defender avoids punishment. It was more accidental rather than malicious.

47: GOAL! Haaland takes just two minutes to rectify his wasteful first half by nodding a header in off the post from Enzo Fernandez's cross.

49: NO PENALTY! City goalkeeper Donnarumma clatters into Porto winger Pepe in the box… but the offside flag goes up against the forward.

57: SO CLOSE! Porto midfielder Alan Varela gets a chance to shoot and curls just wide of the far post. That was Porto's first shot of the game.

66: NERVY! Donnarumma is nearly caught in possession by Porto forward Gomes, but the ball runs behind for a goal kick.

85: JUST WIDE! City substitute Ait-Nouri has the chance to seal the result but steers a shot wide of goal from a good area.

90+1: GOAL! Haaland seals the result by slotting home Ait-Nouri's cutback after he did well to get to the byline.

Should Maresca be happy about Man City's performance?

Man City striker Erling Haaland to Amazon Prime:

"I hope so, we win away in a difficult game. Look at this atmosphere, it was unreal at times. So I hope [yes].

"Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a difficult fight, man against man. They're a top team, impressive, all of them. They play amazing football.

"Well done to them. But with all the pressure, we have to deliver on the biggest stage. That's what we did tonight.

"Honestly we controlled the whole first half. Of course, it's a bit uncomfortable when they come high. But we created a lot of chances. I could have easily had a few more goals.

"But second half we scored and they managed to push us for a good 25 minutes. We managed to hold through and finish the game.

"These are the games we have to win. We had a great start to the season and in the Champions League, you have to win games. If not, you get all the pressure. You never know what's going to happen.

"We have to learn. Enzo has to demand a lot from us and each other. At Man City, you have to win games and win trophies, that's what we have to do."

What the result means and next fixtures...
